title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting processor, the authors implement a hybrid quantum circuit with repeated measurements and feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement measures.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, consistent with theoretical predictions for monitored quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, providing a platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed classically; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states thermalize faster, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect and opens avenues for controlling thermalization in quantum systems.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling limit, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors extend the Keldysh formalism to include Lindblad dissipators, introducing diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism yields a systematic perturbation theory that captures both coherent and dissipative dynamics, enabling the calculation of steady-state properties and fluctuation phenomena in driven open quantum systems.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with direct applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information science.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local quantum state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unbounded resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects by exploring sequential discrimination protocols.
method: The authors analyze sequential local quantum state discrimination protocols where multiple parties perform local measurements on a shared entangled state, and derive conditions under which entanglement is preserved.
result: They prove that there exist protocols where entanglement is sustained for an unbounded number of steps, and the amount of entanglement can be arbitrarily large.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination can be a powerful tool for preserving entanglement, with implications for quantum communication and distributed quantum information processing.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be witnessed despite one wave packet being hidden.
motivation: Understanding whether entanglement can be detected when one party falls into a black hole is fundamental for quantum information in curved spacetime and tests of quantum gravity.
method: The authors analyze a two-mode squeezed state with one mode falling into a Schwarzschild black hole, compute the covariance matrix, and apply an entanglement witness based on the partial transpose criterion.
result: They find that entanglement remains detectable even after one wave packet crosses the event horizon, with the witness value depending on the black hole mass and the wave packet's frequency.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can be witnessed across an event horizon, suggesting that information is not completely lost and providing a potential observable signature of quantum gravity effects.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states (entangled or private) using stabilizer channels, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability.
motivation: Resource states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography but are degraded by noise; distillation protocols are needed to recover high-quality states.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that preserve the stabilizer structure, and derive conditions under which a state can be distilled to a target resource state via such channels.
result: They characterize distillability in terms of the stabilizer group and provide explicit protocols for distilling maximally entangled and private states from noisy ones.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels offer a powerful and general tool for resource state distillation, with implications for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that using a single auxiliary charger can enhance the charging of multimode quantum batteries via daemonic advantage, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by the maximum extractable work (ergotropy). Daemonic advantage, where information from a correlated auxiliary system improves work extraction, has been studied but not fully exploited for charging multimode batteries.
method: The authors consider a protocol where a quantum battery is time-evolved collectively with an auxiliary charger, then the charger is traced out. They define the difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum ergotropy as the 'daemonic gap' and show it can be bridged by optimizing the initial state and interaction.
result: They find that a single auxiliary can bridge the daemonic gap for multimode batteries, enabling extraction of the full ergotropy. The protocol works for various battery sizes and interaction types.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to enhance quantum battery performance using a single auxiliary, advancing the thermodynamics of quantum information processing.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Relaxation And Quantum Mpemba Effect In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Emerson Lima Caldas And Diego Paiva Pires
abstract:
Author(s): Emerson Lima Caldas and Diego Paiva Pires

The Mpemba effect happens when a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster than a system closer to equilibrium. The authors study the relaxation of systems whose effective dynamics are described by Davies maps, providing a framework to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect in Markovian open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012418] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems described by Davies maps, showing that systems initially further from equilibrium can relax faster than those closer to equilibrium.
motivation: The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster. Understanding this effect in quantum systems could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors consider Markovian open quantum systems governed by Davies maps and analyze the relaxation dynamics using spectral properties of the Lindbladian. They derive conditions for the quantum Mpemba effect and provide a framework to engineer it.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect can occur in a wide class of systems and provide explicit examples, showing exponential acceleration of relaxation under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems, which may be useful for quantum thermal machines and control of relaxation processes.

title: Entanglement Recovery By Reversing The Effect Of Noise In A Quantum Repeater
authors: Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, And Seung-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, and Seung-Woo Lee

We propose a method to directly recover the degree of entanglement distributed by entanglement swapping in the presence of noise. Our approach introduces a reversing operation that probabilistically undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012602] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a reversing operation to recover entanglement degraded by amplitude damping or photon loss in quantum repeaters.
motivation: Entanglement swapping in quantum repeaters suffers from noise, reducing the fidelity of distributed entanglement. Existing methods require multiple copies or complex distillation; a direct recovery method is needed.
method: Introduces a probabilistic reversing operation that undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded recovery of entanglement after swapping.
result: The reversing operation can restore the degree of entanglement to near its initial value with a certain success probability, improving the performance of quantum repeaters under realistic noise.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to enhance entanglement distribution in quantum networks, directly addressing noise in quantum repeaters.

title: Quantum Strategies To Overcome Classical Multiplexing Limits
authors: Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Near-term quantum networks face a bottleneck due to low quantum communication rates. This degrades performance both by lowering operating speeds and increasing qubit storage time in noisy memories, making some quantum internet applications infeasible. One way to circumvent this bottleneck is multipl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012603] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes quantum strategies using multiplexing and entanglement to overcome classical multiplexing limits in near-term quantum networks, significantly improving communication rates.
motivation: Near-term quantum networks suffer from low communication rates, which degrade performance and make some quantum internet applications infeasible. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by leveraging quantum resources.
method: The authors develop quantum multiplexing strategies that exploit entanglement and quantum correlations to exceed the classical multiplexing capacity, analyzing their performance in realistic network scenarios.
result: The proposed quantum strategies achieve higher effective communication rates compared to classical multiplexing, reducing qubit storage times and enabling more efficient quantum network operation.
conclusion: Quantum multiplexing offers a practical path to enhance near-term quantum network performance, making quantum internet applications more feasible.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on nonequilibrium work.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium thermodynamics but requires detailed knowledge of the work distribution; a simpler inequality could be more practical for complex systems.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using convexity arguments and apply them to dissipative systems described by Langevin dynamics and field-theoretic models.
result: They obtain bounds on the average exponentiated work that depend only on the dissipation rate or the field-theoretic action, without requiring full distributional information.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities extend the applicability of Jarzynski-type relations to a wider class of systems, offering practical tools for estimating free-energy differences in complex nonequilibrium processes.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations via thermodynamic length in far-from-equilibrium stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems that generalizes the Boltzmann distribution and connects fluctuation relations with thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
method: Derives a thermodynamic length based on the Fisher information metric in the space of probability distributions, and uses it to derive a generalized fluctuation relation and a thermodynamic uncertainty relation.
result: Establishes a unified framework that recovers known fluctuation theorems and uncertainty relations, and provides tighter bounds on current fluctuations in terms of thermodynamic length.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length serves as a unifying concept linking fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, offering new insights into far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their impact on ensemble-based repeaters was not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, considering realistic noise and imperfections. They analyze the entanglement generation rate and fidelity as functions of the number of modes and other parameters.
result: They find that using multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity. The optimal number of modes depends on the specific repeater architecture and noise levels.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising approach to enhance the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing practical long-distance quantum communication closer to realization.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the precision of parameter estimation near quantum phase transitions, accounting for the trade-off between critical enhancement and slowing down.
result: Identifies a universal scaling limit that cannot be surpassed, providing a benchmark for optimal protocols.
conclusion: The bound sets a fundamental limit for critical quantum metrology, guiding the design of optimal estimation strategies.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks, identifying efficient transmission regimes and limitations due to squeezing-induced excitations.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but routing quantum correlations in a controlled manner remains challenging. This work aims to achieve directional entanglement transport using nonreciprocal coupling.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with nonreciprocal couplings and analyze entanglement propagation using covariance matrix formalism and logarithmic negativity.
result: They identify a parameter regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted through the network, and show that strong squeezing introduces excess excitations that ultimately limit the routing mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing in continuous-variable quantum networks, with practical trade-offs between transmission efficiency and noise from squeezing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond, coupled single tin-vacancy centers to the cavity mode, and measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and high-fidelity entanglement generation capability.
conclusion: This platform is promising for scalable quantum network nodes, enabling high-rate entanglement distribution over long distances.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, which has implications for understanding quantum resources.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: They show that many standard signatures of quantumness are recovered, and that certain processes long considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features.
conclusion: The work refines our understanding of quantumness and may guide the identification of useful quantum resources for technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a dissipative protocol where spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity, and by engineering the dissipation (e.g., through cavity loss and drive), they stabilize desired entangled states without requiring precise initial state preparation.
result: The scheme produces reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, Dicke states) that are robust against certain imperfections, and they show applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, including entropy accumulation and finite-size effects, to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is both secure and efficient, paving the way for real-world deployment of high-rate quantum key distribution.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, contrasting with the polynomial decay without recording. This reveals a measurement-induced phase transition in information lifetime.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes can dramatically extend quantum information lifetime, offering a practical strategy for preserving fragile quantum data in near-term devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They observe that ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: New mitigation strategies beyond conventional shielding are needed to protect superconducting qubits from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their preparation typically incurs high overhead. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to parallelize the distillation process.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to conventional magic-state distillation protocols, making it more suitable for near-term quantum architectures.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path toward low-overhead universal quantum computing, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A complete SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on non-classical resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification of non-projective measurements, and the experimental demonstration validates the theoretical method.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, which is important for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating as an autonomous machine.
method: The authors model a quantum particle detector as an autonomous thermal machine, analyzing its dynamics using stochastic thermodynamics and information theory. They derive trade-off relations between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental thermodynamic bound on information acquisition. The model demonstrates a clear trade-off between the detector's performance and its thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational understanding of the thermodynamics of quantum measurement, with implications for designing energy-efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating decoherence in solid-state emitters is essential.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms, likely including temperature and electric field effects.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and demonstrate improved stability through cavity enhancement, achieving narrow linewidths suitable for quantum networking.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, with spectral stability that can be controlled and optimized.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements in a quantum error-correcting code can improve decoding performance by leveraging measurement outcomes.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze a quantum code subject to random projective measurements and develop a decoding algorithm that uses measurement outcomes to correct errors.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes significantly enhances decodability, leading to improved logical error rates compared to unmonitored codes.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising approach for robust quantum information processing by exploiting measurement feedback.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, achieving miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. An integrated photonic solution is needed for practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing QRNG protocol based on Bell inequality violation, integrating all necessary optical components on a single chip.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with a certified min-entropy rate, demonstrating the first fully integrated self-testing QRNG with performance suitable for real-world applications.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices by combining device-independent security with integrated photonics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. The authors aim to improve near-term feasibility.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the required number of emitters and improves loss tolerance, making quantum repeaters more practical with current technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a promising path toward scalable and efficient quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence time and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are promising for scalable quantum technologies, but suitable spin defects with long coherence and high readout fidelity have been lacking.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental and theoretical methods, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: They find an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization data, allowing for practical security bounds.
result: The framework yields rigorous security guarantees that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits with erasure conversion offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the feasibility of scalable superconducting quantum processors.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches and connects microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic laws.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified thermodynamic description across scales, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights into nonequilibrium phenomena.

title: Freeness Reined In By A Single Qubit
authors: Alexander Altland, Francisco Divi, Tobias Micklitz, And Maedeh Rezaei
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Altland, Francisco Divi, Tobias Micklitz, and Maedeh Rezaei

Free probability provides a framework for describing correlations between noncommuting observables in complex quantum systems whose Hilbert-space states follow maximum-entropy distributions. We examine the robustness of this framework under a minimal deviation from freeness: the coupling of a single…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines the robustness of free probability in describing correlations in complex quantum systems when a single qubit is coupled, showing that freeness is fragile.
motivation: Free probability is a powerful tool for analyzing noncommuting observables in large quantum systems, but its validity under minimal perturbations is unclear. The authors test this by coupling a single qubit to a free system.
method: The authors analyze a model where a large free system is coupled to a single qubit, using random matrix theory and free probability techniques to compute correlation functions and deviations from freeness.
result: They find that even a single qubit coupling destroys freeness, leading to non-vanishing correlations that scale with system size, and characterize the resulting structure using a diagrammatic expansion.
conclusion: Freeness is not robust to minimal perturbations, implying that many-body quantum systems with local interactions are generally not free, which has implications for quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Genuinely Nonlocal Sets With Smallest Cardinality
authors: Zong-Xing Xiong, Mao-Sheng Li, Bing Yu, Zhu-Jun Zheng, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zong-Xing Xiong, Mao-Sheng Li, Bing Yu, Zhu-Jun Zheng, and Lvzhou Li

Recently, there has been growing interest in the study of genuine nonlocality, which serves to explore the local accessibility of global information encoded in orthogonal multipartite quantum states under scenarios where not all subsystems are joined together. For this form of nonlocality, a probabl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012410] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies the smallest cardinality of genuinely nonlocal sets of orthogonal multipartite quantum states, proving that for n-partite systems with local dimension d, the minimum size is 2n-1.
motivation: Genuine nonlocality captures the local accessibility of global information in multipartite quantum states. Determining the minimal size of genuinely nonlocal sets is a fundamental open problem.
method: The authors construct explicit sets of orthogonal multipartite states with size 2n-1 and prove that no smaller set can be genuinely nonlocal using combinatorial and information-theoretic arguments.
result: The minimal cardinality of a genuinely nonlocal set in an n-partite system with local dimension d is exactly 2n-1, independent of d (for d≥2).
conclusion: This tight bound resolves a key question in the study of genuine nonlocality and provides a clear benchmark for future work on local accessibility of multipartite quantum information.

title: Unbounded Sequence Of Observers Exhibiting Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering Via Probabilistic Projective Measurements
authors: Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, And Hui-Juan Zuo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, and Hui-Juan Zuo

Recent studies have demonstrated that coherent weak measurements allow Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering to be shared sequentially between a single Alice and multiple Bobs. Theoretically, this permits an unbounded sequence in the high-dimensional limit. In this work, we investigate whether the experi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012411] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering can be shared among an unbounded sequence of observers using probabilistic projective measurements, extending previous results with weak measurements.
motivation: To determine whether the sequential sharing of EPR steering can be achieved with projective measurements, which are more experimentally accessible than weak measurements, and to explore the theoretical limits on the number of observers.
method: The authors propose a protocol using probabilistic projective measurements on one side of a bipartite entangled state, allowing multiple Bobs to sequentially demonstrate steering with a single Alice. They analyze the trade-off between the number of observers and the violation of steering inequalities.
result: They prove that an unbounded number of Bobs can sequentially demonstrate steering in the limit of high-dimensional entangled states, and provide explicit examples with qubit and qutrit systems showing finite sequences.
conclusion: Probabilistic projective measurements can replace weak measurements for sequential steering, enabling an unbounded sequence of observers in principle, which has implications for quantum communication and foundational tests.

title: Temporal Steering Of Entanglement Decay With Single-shot Control
authors: Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, And Urbasi Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, and Urbasi Sinha

Entanglement in open quantum systems can vanish abruptly through entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution, posing a challenge for quantum technologies. Here, we show that the timing of a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the trajectory of entanglement deca…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012416] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a single local unitary operation can steer the trajectory of entanglement decay in open quantum systems, enabling control over entanglement sudden death.
motivation: Entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution poses a challenge for quantum technologies; controlling entanglement decay is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate that the timing of a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the entanglement decay trajectory in a two-qubit system coupled to a dissipative environment.
result: They show that by applying a local unitary at a specific time, they can either accelerate or delay entanglement sudden death, effectively steering the entanglement evolution.
conclusion: This work provides a method for temporal control of entanglement decay, which could be useful for quantum information processing in noisy environments.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurement devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement device to characterize and then purify noisy preparation and measurement operations, leveraging a series of quantum state tomography and error mitigation techniques.
result: The protocol effectively reduces preparation and measurement errors, improving the fidelity of quantum operations without requiring full quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to enhance the quality of qubit operations in near-term quantum devices, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum networks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction scheme that protects against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, exploiting the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated and transferred between nuclear qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, high-efficiency photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms.
method: Design and fabrication of an on-chip parabolic mirror with fiber in/out coupling, integrated with neutral atoms.
result: Demonstrated efficient photon extraction and compact, stable operation suitable for quantum network nodes.
conclusion: The device provides a practical platform for future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions, comparing with standard readout techniques.
result: The nonlinear coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical way to improve transmon readout, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a theoretical framework linking it to state compression and measurement complexity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a valid resource measure that is additive under tensor products and provides tight bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and optimizing continuous-variable quantum information protocols, with implications for quantum computing and communication.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and minimal disturbance remains challenging. Existing methods often involve destructive imaging or require complex setups.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays. They use a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio and enable continuous loading.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays with low atom loss and minimal heating, achieving a significant improvement over previous techniques.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging provides a practical and scalable method for real-time monitoring and control of neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which combine cavity QED and Rydberg atoms, is of fundamental interest for quantum simulation and many-body physics.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays with kinetic constraints arising from Rydberg blockade, using analytical and numerical methods to analyze the phase diagram and dynamics.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, which are robust signatures of non-ergodic behavior in a driven-dissipative setting.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cavity-mediated interactions in Rydberg arrays can produce novel non-equilibrium phases, relevant for quantum simulation and quantum information platforms.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents, finite-size scaling, and dynamical responses near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance the quantum Fisher information and achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in estimation precision.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust and practical route to high-precision metrology, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced measurements.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences typically scale poorly with qubit number for correlated noise; this work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging coding theory to generate sequences that cancel spatially correlated noise up to k-body interactions.
result: They produce sequences whose length depends only on the code parameters and not on the total qubit count, enabling efficient decoupling for large systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a practical tool for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently identifies hidden subgroups in Abelian groups from quantum states, unifying several symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a cavity-mode multiplexing technique to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, addressing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms. Scaling to large arrays requires parallel processing.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously interact with different atoms in the array, leveraging spatial mode multiplexing to achieve parallel operations.
result: They demonstrate that cavity-mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms that can be processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity enhancement, enabling scalable quantum operations.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing offers a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom arrays, advancing the platform toward large-scale quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing how entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization And Spectral Imprints Of Many-body Systems In Projected Local Observables
authors: Shivam Mishra, C Jisha, And Ravi Prakash
abstract:
Author(s): Shivam Mishra, C Jisha, and Ravi Prakash

The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis explains thermalization in isolated quantum systems through the statistical properties of observables in the energy eigenbasis. We study the crossover from integrability-to-chaos in the spin-[MATH] XXZ chain by introducing a local perturbation. Using exact dia…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) in the spin-1/2 XXZ chain with a local perturbation, examining the crossover from integrability to chaos via projected local observables.
motivation: Understanding thermalization in isolated quantum systems is a central problem in quantum thermodynamics. The ETH provides a framework, but its signatures in local observables during the integrability-to-chaos transition are not fully characterized.
method: The authors introduce a local perturbation to the integrable XXZ chain and perform exact diagonalization to compute matrix elements of local observables in the energy eigenbasis. They analyze statistical properties such as the variance and distribution of off-diagonal elements.
result: They find clear signatures of the crossover in the spectral statistics of projected local observables, including a transition from Poisson to Wigner-Dyson distributions and scaling behavior consistent with ETH predictions.
conclusion: The results confirm that projected local observables can serve as sensitive probes of the integrability-to-chaos transition, providing a practical tool for diagnosing thermalization in many-body systems.
