title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems constantly dissipate energy, and extending this paradigm to quantum systems requires a proper description of the environment and dissipation, which is currently lacking.
method: The authors derive a general theoretical framework based on open quantum systems and master equations to model dissipation in quantum active matter, incorporating both coherent and dissipative dynamics.
result: They obtain a set of equations that describe the non-equilibrium steady states and dynamics of quantum active matter, showing how dissipation leads to directed motion and pattern formation.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter and highlights the role of dissipation in driving non-equilibrium quantum phenomena, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Distributed Quantum Dense Coding Enhanced With Nonclassical Routing
authors: Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We propose a distributed quantum dense coding protocol that uses a control system to superpose two dense coding processes, allowing us to simultaneously and coherently encode and nonclassically route the sender's single-qubit system to two receiver laboratories. We find that dense coding with cohere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012605] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distributed quantum dense coding protocol with nonclassical routing using a control system to superpose two dense coding processes.
motivation: To enhance quantum dense coding by enabling simultaneous encoding and coherent routing of a single-qubit system to two receivers, improving communication efficiency.
method: The protocol uses a control qubit to create a superposition of two dense coding processes, allowing the sender's qubit to be nonclassically routed to two receiver laboratories.
result: The protocol achieves higher information capacity than standard dense coding and demonstrates nonclassical routing advantages.
conclusion: Distributed quantum dense coding with nonclassical routing offers a new approach for quantum communication networks, potentially improving multi-party quantum information transfer.

title: Three-dimensional Squeezing Of Optically Levitated Nanospheres
authors: Giacomo Marocco, David C. Moore, And Daniel Carney
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Marocco, David C. Moore, and Daniel Carney

We propose a protocol to measure three-dimensional impulses beyond the standard quantum limit. The protocol reduces noise in all three spatial dimensions and consists of squeezing a mechanical system's state via a series of jumps in the frequency of the harmonic potential. We quantify how decoherenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for three-dimensional squeezing of optically levitated nanospheres to measure impulses beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Optically levitated nanospheres are promising for force sensing but limited by quantum noise; squeezing can enhance sensitivity.
method: The protocol uses a series of jumps in the harmonic potential frequency to squeeze the mechanical state in all three spatial dimensions, and accounts for decoherence.
result: The protocol reduces noise in all three dimensions, enabling measurement of three-dimensional impulses beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum-enhanced sensing with levitated nanoparticles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parity Readout In Majorana Box Qubits From The Dispersive To The Resonant Regime
authors: Sara M. Benjadi And Reinhold Egger
abstract:
Author(s): Sara M. Benjadi and Reinhold Egger

We study theoretical models for charge reflectometry and capacitive readout of the Majorana parity degree of freedom in Majorana box qubits, considering decoherence channels within the framework of the Lindblad master equation. Noting that a parity-dependent dynamical susceptibility [MATH] gov…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034503] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies parity readout of Majorana box qubits using charge reflectometry, analyzing decoherence via Lindblad master equation.
motivation: Majorana box qubits are a promising topological qubit platform, but reliable parity readout is essential for quantum computing. This work aims to understand readout mechanisms and decoherence channels.
method: The authors model charge reflectometry and capacitive readout of the Majorana parity, using a parity-dependent dynamical susceptibility and Lindblad master equation to account for decoherence.
result: They characterize the readout signal from the dispersive to the resonant regime, showing how decoherence affects the parity readout fidelity.
conclusion: The study provides theoretical insights into optimizing parity readout for Majorana box qubits, which is relevant for topological quantum computing hardware.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models using thermodynamic principles, particularly by breaking detailed balance to accelerate sampling and enhance learning.
method: The authors analyze generative models from a nonequilibrium perspective, demonstrating that breaking detailed balance leads to latent cycles that improve learning dynamics.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, beyond merely correcting slow equilibrium mixing.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a useful framework for designing and understanding generative models, with practical benefits for machine learning.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: Understanding how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior is of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a dynamical phase transition.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that resetting and measurements can profoundly alter the thermodynamic behavior of many-body systems, with implications for control and information processing.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical learning on randomized measurement data to verify approximate k-designs in quantum states.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for applications like benchmarking and studying thermalization, but direct verification is costly.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on randomized measurements and classical machine learning to certify approximate k-designs without full state tomography.
result: They demonstrate that their method can efficiently distinguish k-designs from non-design ensembles using limited measurement data.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for verifying random state ensembles, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding the statistics of fluctuations in large regions after quantum quenches is a fundamental challenge in non-equilibrium physics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body systems.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of charge transfer in integrable systems, treating the quench as a source of ballistic transport and deriving large-deviation formulas.
result: They obtain exact results for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations follow a universal scaling form, with the variance growing linearly in time and higher cumulants exhibiting specific power laws.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for fluctuation statistics in non-equilibrium integrable systems, bridging quantum quenches and thermodynamic fluctuation theory.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over the ion's motional state via laser pulses, enabling the synthesis of arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a key tool for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum computing and networking applications.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: The proposed photonic simulator is highly configurable and can efficiently simulate various quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a practical photonic platform for quantum simulation, advancing hybrid quantum systems for field theory applications.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard approaches in efficiency.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum model learning and adaptive estimation in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum control tasks compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome performance limits in large-scale quantum processors, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely through optimized circuit parameters and materials.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking traditional performance limits for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in hybrid quantum systems where microwave-to-optical conversion or signal amplification is required.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less explored; this review aims to classify and assess them.
method: The authors categorize quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and analyze their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a structured overview of the capabilities and limitations of various quantum cryptographic primitives, highlighting experimental progress and open challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich landscape beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant hurdles; further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior in driven open many-body systems, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to symmetry and topological invariants.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, offering a foundation for understanding nonequilibrium stationary states.

title: $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-Symmetric Magnon Lasing And Antilasing
authors: Xi-Guang Wang, Tian-Xiang Lu, Guang-Hua Guo, Jamal Berakdar, And Hui Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-guang Wang, Tian-xiang Lu, Guang-hua Guo, Jamal Berakdar, and Hui Jing

A mechanism for electrically tunable [MATH]-symmetric magnonic lasing and antilasing is proposed along with a device consisting of a current-biased region in a magnetically ordered planar waveguide. Within the bias area, several heavy-metal wires carrying dc charge currents are per…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026701] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a mechanism for electrically tunable PT-symmetric magnon lasing and antilasing in a planar waveguide with heavy-metal wires.
motivation: To achieve controllable magnon lasing and antilasing, which are important for spintronic and magnonic devices.
method: Theoretical proposal using a current-biased region in a magnetically ordered planar waveguide with heavy-metal wires carrying dc currents to induce PT symmetry.
result: Demonstrates electrically tunable PT-symmetric magnon lasing and antilasing.
conclusion: The proposed device offers a new way to control magnon dynamics with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Microscopic Rydberg Electron Orbit Manipulation With Optical Tweezers
authors: Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, And Florian Meinert
abstract:
Author(s): Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, and Florian Meinert

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. Here, we propose the local manipulation and spatiotemporal sculpting of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes local manipulation of Rydberg electron orbitals using optical tweezers to create tailored long-range interactions.
motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: Theoretical proposal combining optical tweezers with Rydberg excitation to locally control electron orbitals via Stark shifts and dipole forces.
result: Demonstrates that optical tweezers can reshape Rydberg electron orbitals, enabling tunable anisotropic interactions between atoms.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for engineering quantum many-body systems with controllable long-range interactions.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method for neutral atom qubits achieves high fidelity at the single-photon level, reducing resource requirements for scalable quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage qubit readout, but fluorescence-based readout at the single-photon level suffers from low signal-to-noise ratio.
method: The authors combine a Bayesian estimator with a neural network trained on experimental data to infer qubit state from sparse photon counts, optimizing readout fidelity under short exposure times.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with only a few photons per shot, significantly outperforming conventional thresholding and reducing atom loss.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical, resource-efficient readout technique that can be integrated into large-scale neutral atom quantum processors, advancing the platform's scalability.

title: Doubling Qubits In A Trapped-ion System Via Vibrational Dual-rail Encoding
authors: Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, And Joonsuk Huh
abstract:
Author(s): Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, and Joonsuk Huh

Vibrational modes of trapped ions have traditionally served as quantum buses to mediate entanglement between internal qubits. However, with recent advances in quantum control, it has become possible to use these modes directly as quantum computational resources. Here, we propose a dual-rail encoding…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a dual-rail encoding using vibrational modes of trapped ions to double the number of qubits without increasing ion count.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum computers face scalability limits due to the number of ions required. Using vibrational modes as qubits can increase computational resources without adding more ions.
method: The authors propose encoding qubits in the vibrational modes of trapped ions using a dual-rail scheme, where each ion's motional states represent a logical qubit, and they analyze the required control techniques.
result: The dual-rail encoding effectively doubles the number of available qubits in a trapped-ion system, with potential for high-fidelity operations using existing control methods.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to increase qubit count in trapped-ion systems, leveraging vibrational modes as quantum resources, and is compatible with current experimental capabilities.

title: Tunneling Of Bosonic Qubits Under Local Dephasing Through A Microscopic Approach
authors: Alberto Ferrara, Farzam Nosrati, Andrea Smirne, Jyrki Piilo, And Rosario Lo Franco
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Ferrara, Farzam Nosrati, Andrea Smirne, Jyrki Piilo, and Rosario Lo Franco

We present a microscopic derivation of a master equation for two-component bosons (bosonic qubits) which tunnel between spatially separated modes under local dephasing noise. Starting from the full system-bath Hamiltonian with Lorentzian coupling distributions, we analytically obtain a time-local ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012415] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic master equation for bosonic qubits tunneling under local dephasing is derived, revealing non-Markovian dynamics and decoherence suppression.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in bosonic qubits is crucial for quantum information processing; a microscopic approach captures non-Markovian effects missed by phenomenological models.
method: Starting from a full system-bath Hamiltonian with Lorentzian coupling, the authors analytically derive a time-local master equation for two-component bosons tunneling between spatially separated modes.
result: The derived master equation shows that local dephasing can be suppressed by tunneling, and non-Markovianity is quantified via the trace distance.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for analyzing decoherence in bosonic qubits, with implications for quantum memory and communication.

title: Quantum Resource Theory Of $π$-ordered Coherence
authors: Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, And Jinchuan Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, and Jinchuan Hou

Within the framework of resource theory, the research on quantum coherence has not only furnished a rigorous and systematic methodology for investigating quantum coherence and developing coherence quantification methods, but also tackled key issues regarding the conversion and practical utilization …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012417] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for π-ordered coherence, a specific type of quantum coherence, and provides a complete set of monotones and conversion conditions.
motivation: Quantum coherence is a key resource in quantum information, but most resource theories focus on standard coherence. This work aims to formalize π-ordered coherence, which arises in contexts like quantum metrology and thermodynamics, to enable rigorous quantification and manipulation.
method: The authors define π-ordered coherence within the resource theory framework, identifying free operations and states. They construct a family of monotones based on the Schatten p-norms and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for state conversion under these operations.
result: They obtain a complete set of monotones that characterize π-ordered coherence and derive conditions for when one state can be converted to another via free operations. The results generalize known results for standard coherence.
conclusion: The resource theory of π-ordered coherence is fully characterized, providing tools for studying coherence in ordered bases, which may have applications in quantum information processing tasks that involve phase references or timekeeping.

title: Energy-time Attack On Detectors In Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, And Vadim Makarov
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, and Vadim Makarov

Quantum key distribution is unbreakable in theory but may be hacked via imperfections in its hardware implementations. While many imperfections have been mitigated by countermeasures and advanced security proofs, several remain unsolved. One of these is a superlinear behavior in single-photon detect…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012601] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and demonstrates an energy-time side-channel attack on single-photon detectors in QKD systems, exploiting superlinear detection efficiency to compromise security.
motivation: Practical QKD implementations have hardware imperfections that can be exploited by eavesdroppers; this work addresses a previously unmitigated vulnerability in single-photon detectors.
method: The authors analyze the superlinear response of single-photon detectors to energy-time correlated pulses and design an attack that uses tailored bright pulses to force detection events that leak key information.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the attack on a commercial QKD system, showing that an eavesdropper can gain partial or full key information without being detected by standard monitoring.
conclusion: The energy-time attack poses a realistic threat to QKD security, and countermeasures such as detector shielding or modified detection schemes are necessary to close this loophole.

title: Collective Vibronic Cascade In Cavity-coupled Jahn-Teller Active Molecules
authors: Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, And Krishna R. Nandipati
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, and Krishna R. Nandipati

We study the polaritonic states and dynamics of multiple Jahn-Teller (JT) active molecules coupled to the modes of a Fabry-Perot cavity. We find that collective effects dramatically alter the interplay of electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta, giving rise to markedly different polarito…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012802] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective vibronic cascades in cavity-coupled Jahn-Teller active molecules, revealing how collective effects alter polaritonic states and dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the interplay of electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta in molecular systems coupled to optical cavities is crucial for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze multiple Jahn-Teller active molecules coupled to Fabry-Perot cavity modes, using a model that incorporates collective effects and angular momentum coupling.
result: Collective effects dramatically change the polaritonic states, leading to markedly different dynamics compared to single-molecule or uncoupled scenarios.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling molecular quantum systems via cavity coupling, relevant for quantum networking and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Subradiant Collective States For Precision Sensing Via Transmission Spectra
authors: Diego Zafra-Bono, Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, And Susanne F. Yelin
abstract:
Author(s): Diego Zafra-Bono, Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, and Susanne F. Yelin

The authors propose a quantum metrology framework that harnesses the narrow linewidths of subradiant collective states in subwavelength emitter arrays. By introducing spatially varying control detunings to couple dark and bright modes, they show that the resulting sharp features in the transmission spectrum enable the precise detection of both global and local perturbations under realistic experimental imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013704] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using subradiant collective states in subwavelength emitter arrays for precision sensing via transmission spectra.
motivation: Subradiant states have narrow linewidths that are sensitive to perturbations, but they are dark and cannot be directly probed. The authors aim to harness these states for metrology by coupling them to bright modes.
method: They introduce spatially varying control detunings to couple dark subradiant modes to bright superradiant modes, creating sharp features in the transmission spectrum that can be used to detect perturbations.
result: The proposed scheme enables precise detection of both global and local perturbations, and is robust to realistic experimental imperfections such as position disorder and finite array size.
conclusion: Subradiant collective states in emitter arrays offer a promising platform for quantum sensing, leveraging narrow linewidths for high precision.

title: Nonequilibrium (thermo)dynamics Of Colloids Under Mobile Piston Compression
authors: Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, And Joachim Dzubiella
abstract:
Author(s): Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, and Joachim Dzubiella

We investigate the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile boundary within dynamical density functional theory. The system consists of a hard-sphere fluid confined between two parallel walls, one of which acts as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015403] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile piston using dynamical density functional theory.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamics and dynamics of soft matter under nonequilibrium conditions is important for both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The authors employ dynamical density functional theory to model a hard-sphere fluid confined between two walls, with one wall acting as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase in external force.
result: They analyze the time-dependent density profiles, piston motion, and thermodynamic quantities such as work and heat during the compression process.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of colloidal systems under mechanical compression, relevant to information thermodynamics and soft matter physics.

title: Score-based Modeling Of Effective Langevin Dynamics
authors: Ludovico Theo Giorgini
abstract:
Author(s): Ludovico Theo Giorgini

We introduce a constructive framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series. Unlike conventional approaches that require iterative calibration to match target statistics, our construction guarantees the observed steady-state density by design and enforces short-lag coordi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series that guarantees the observed steady-state density by design.
motivation: Conventional approaches require iterative calibration to match target statistics; this work aims to construct effective dynamics that directly reproduce the observed stationary distribution.
method: The authors propose a score-based modeling approach that enforces the steady-state density and short-lag correlations, leveraging score matching techniques.
result: The method yields effective Langevin equations that accurately capture the stationary statistics and short-time dynamics of the original system.
conclusion: This framework provides a principled and efficient way to infer effective stochastic dynamics from data, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active fluctuations.
motivation: The ratchet principle traditionally states that directed currents require violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries. The authors aim to test this principle in active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials.
method: They study stochastic dynamics in asymmetric potentials, comparing passive (thermal) noise with active (colored) noise, and analyze the conditions for steady-state currents using symmetry arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They find that active fluctuations can break detailed balance and generate directed currents even when all symmetries are preserved, challenging the traditional ratchet principle. Passive systems require symmetry breaking for currents.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be refined for active systems: active noise can induce currents without symmetry violation, highlighting the role of non-equilibrium fluctuations in directed transport.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Rydberg blockade near Förster resonance.
motivation: To develop a sensitive electric field gradiometer that exploits the strong dependence of Rydberg blockade on electric fields.
method: Uses networks of Rydberg atoms where the blockade radius changes with applied electric field near a Förster resonance, enabling local field variation detection.
result: Demonstrates that the sensor can measure electric field gradients with high sensitivity, leveraging collective Rydberg excitations.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks provide a promising platform for electric field gradiometry with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and using atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and information processing; generating it in a hybrid system combining atomic ensembles and optical fields is of interest.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved optical mode.
result: The scheme can produce significant squeezing (e.g., 3 dB) under realistic experimental parameters, with the amount depending on storage time and atomic density.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a new method for generating squeezed light using existing BEC and quantum memory technology, potentially useful for quantum networks and metrology.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, and Petr Marek

The one-way quantum computation utilizing bosonic modes of light offers unmatched scalability of light modes, and it has seen rapid experimental development recently. Scalability requires robust and low-error gates and measurements. Squeezing gate is one of the necessary Gaussian operations. We find…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a teleportation-based squeezer for bosonic cluster states to improve scalability in one-way quantum computing.
motivation: One-way quantum computation with bosonic modes requires robust and low-error gates; squeezing is a necessary Gaussian operation that currently limits scalability.
method: The authors design a teleportation-based squeezing gate that uses ancillary squeezed states and homodyne measurements to implement squeezing on cluster states.
result: The proposed squeezer achieves high fidelity and success probability, reducing the resource overhead compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This teleportation-based squeezer enhances the feasibility of scalable bosonic cluster-state quantum computing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum synchronization in a controlled platform and explore its potential for quantum information processing.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators.
result: Synchronization is observed through a fixed relative phase accessible only via joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle for quantum synchronization in trapped ions, relevant for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in many quantum systems but are computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a rigorous and efficient approach.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and scalable tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further development.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, benchmarking against classical simulations to quantify the advantage.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable for simulating entangled many-body dynamics, with performance exceeding classical capabilities.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating complex quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise and decoherence; differential phase sensing requires common-mode noise rejection to achieve practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for generating and manipulating Lieb-Mattis states in spin ensembles, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation under realistic noise.
result: Lieb-Mattis states provide Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being intrinsically insensitive to common-mode fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states offer a practical route to scalable quantum sensor networks by combining entanglement-enhanced metrology with built-in noise robustness.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and continuum limits that bridge jump and diffusion descriptions.
result: Establishes a unified stochastic calculus that recovers known results for diffusion processes and provides new tools for jump processes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of pathwise thermodynamic quantities in systems with discrete state spaces, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for systematic optimization of quantum light sources, significantly increasing the success rate of generating essential quantum states.
motivation: Generating non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods suffer from low success rates. The authors aim to develop a systematic optimization framework to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank, enabling scalable optimization of optical non-Gaussian state generation. They likely use numerical optimization and experimental validation.
result: The new control parameters allow orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach to non-Gaussian state generation, which is important for quantum computing and communication applications.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage to highly excited states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize the excited-state dynamics of transmon qubits, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They observe and quantify the ionization process, showing how qubits escape the computational subspace through specific resonance conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform better readout and error mitigation strategies for superconducting qubits.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and comparing to theoretical models of blackbody-induced transitions.
result: At cryogenic temperatures (∼4 K), Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, significantly reducing the dominant relaxation error source.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to improve neutral-atom quantum gate fidelities, potentially enabling fault-tolerant quantum computing with Rydberg arrays.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting without explicit regularization.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and it is unclear whether quantum neural networks have similar limitations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the parameter update dynamics of quantum neural networks and perform numerical experiments on continual learning benchmarks.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain high plasticity even as parameters grow, significantly outperforming classical networks in retaining previously learned tasks.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks offer a natural advantage for continual learning due to their intrinsic parameter structure, suggesting potential for lifelong learning applications.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them to perform displacement sensing, analyzing the metrological advantage.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that numerically optimizes control pulses to implement multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) with high fidelity, accounting for realistic experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate that optimized pulses can achieve fidelities exceeding 99.9% for three-qubit gates, significantly outperforming naive implementations.
conclusion: The framework enables practical multiqubit gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom systems, advancing the viability of these platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods, enabling practical quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and efficient quantum algorithm for simulating nonunitary processes, with applications in quantum information and open quantum systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, filling the intermediate-frequency gap and providing a more complete noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise spectroscopy in qubit platforms, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve robust photon blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission properties as a function of system size.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without introducing additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer tailored optical interactions in a fully optical system to create an effective negative-mass oscillator that coherently cancels quantum backaction.
result: They demonstrate coherent quantum noise cancellation, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive. Reducing the overhead of Hamiltonian simulation can make phase estimation more practical.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps to approximate the time evolution operator with lower error and cost.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard product formulas, while maintaining rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution is a practical technique to slash the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of diverse methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various numerical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical contexts.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis facilitate the application of non-Markovian simulation methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits can reduce the complexity of quantum circuits by replacing multiple qubits with a single higher-dimensional system, potentially improving scalability and error rates.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates and offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing, though challenges in qudit control and coherence remain.
conclusion: Qudits are a valuable resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit depth and enabling algorithms on current hardware, but further development is needed for full-scale quantum computers.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is a key challenge. The paper aims to establish confidence in ab initio predictions of decoherence for various spin qubit platforms.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches to model spin-spin relaxation, including higher-order perturbation effects and surface/interface contributions.
result: Cluster expansion methods have matured to reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits, though challenges remain for cases with higher-order perturbations or surface-driven decoherence.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of solid-state spin qubits with improved coherence times.

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Characterization Of A Two-Channel Optical Network Via Two-Port Homodyne Detection
authors: Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, And Vincenzo Tamma
abstract:
Author(s): Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, and Vincenzo Tamma

We present a fully Gaussian and experimentally feasible scheme for the simultaneous estimation of the four real parameters that characterize a two-channel optical network. The scheme utilizes a two-mode squeezed probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports, for which we derive the comp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010801] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A Gaussian scheme for simultaneous estimation of four parameters of a two-channel optical network using two-mode squeezed light and homodyne detection achieves Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Characterizing multiparameter quantum optical networks is important for quantum information processing, but achieving optimal scaling simultaneously for all parameters is challenging.
method: The scheme uses a two-mode squeezed vacuum probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports; the Fisher information matrix is derived analytically to assess estimation precision.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling for all four parameters simultaneously, with the Fisher information matrix being diagonal and independent of the unknown parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, fully Gaussian approach for multiparameter estimation in optical networks, relevant for quantum metrology and network characterization.

title: Squeezing Properties And Parameter Estimation In A Driven Swanson Oscillator Damped In A Thermal Reservoir
authors: Jing-Yang Li And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-yang Li and Yaping Yang

The quadrature squeezing and quantum Fisher information in a driven non-Hermitian Swanson oscillator coupled to a thermal bath are studied. Analytically solving the master equation, we find that the system reaches a Gaussian steady state in the [MATH]-symmetric regime. Quadrature squeezing a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013706] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quadrature squeezing and quantum Fisher information in a driven non-Hermitian Swanson oscillator coupled to a thermal bath, finding Gaussian steady states in the PT-symmetric regime.
motivation: Understanding squeezing and parameter estimation in non-Hermitian quantum systems is important for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The authors analytically solve the master equation for the driven Swanson oscillator damped in a thermal reservoir, deriving the steady-state covariance matrix and quantum Fisher information.
result: Quadrature squeezing is observed in the PT-symmetric regime, and the quantum Fisher information shows enhanced sensitivity near the exceptional point.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that non-Hermitian systems can exhibit useful squeezing and metrological properties, relevant for quantum thermodynamical applications.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method to classically simulate small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly. The authors aim to efficiently surrogate local patches of these landscapes.
method: They develop a classical surrogate model that approximates the expectation value landscape in a local region by leveraging a small amount of quantum measurement data, using techniques from classical shadow tomography and polynomial approximation.
result: The method achieves accurate predictions of expectation values within a local patch with significantly reduced quantum and classical resources compared to full simulation, and they provide theoretical guarantees on the approximation error.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for analyzing and optimizing variational quantum circuits by enabling efficient classical surrogates of local landscape patches, which can aid in understanding trainability and avoiding barren plateaus.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
