title: Machine Learning Of Topological Insulator And Anderson Insulator In The One-dimensional Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Zhekai Yin And C. K. Ong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhekai Yin and C. K. Ong

We study disorder effects in the extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model using a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on reduced correlation matrices (RCMs) of disorder-free systems to predict winding number phase diagrams in systems with off-diagonal and diagonal disorder. The trained CNN model g…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to classify topological and Anderson insulators in a disordered SSH chain, focusing on phase diagrams rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To demonstrate that a convolutional neural network trained on disorder-free reduced correlation matrices can predict winding number phase diagrams in disordered systems, bypassing traditional topological invariants.
method: A CNN is trained on reduced correlation matrices of clean SSH chains and then applied to systems with off-diagonal and diagonal disorder to predict topological phases.
result: The CNN accurately predicts the winding number phase diagram even in the presence of disorder, distinguishing topological insulator phases from Anderson insulator phases.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively classify topological phases in disordered systems using correlation matrices, offering a new tool for studying topological matter.

title: Many-body non-Hermitian Quasiperiodic Systems With Power-law Hopping: Localization, Topology, And The Skin Effect
authors: Aditi Chakrabarty, Sanchayan Banerjee, Tapan Mishra, And Sanjoy Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Aditi Chakrabarty, Sanchayan Banerjee, Tapan Mishra, and Sanjoy Datta

In this work, we study one-dimensional interacting non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices with asymmetric power-law hopping in the presence of time-reversal symmetry (TRS). In contrast to earlier works on short-range non-Hermitian quasiperiodic models with TRS, both with and without interactions, wher…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems with power-law hopping, focusing on localization, topology, and skin effects.
motivation: To understand the interplay of non-Hermiticity, quasiperiodicity, and long-range hopping in many-body systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional interacting non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice with asymmetric power-law hopping under time-reversal symmetry, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that power-law hopping modifies localization properties and induces novel topological phases and skin effects.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems to long-range interactions, revealing new phenomena.

title: Inelastic Neutron Scattering Signatures Of Chiral Phonons
authors: Tingting Wang, Jun Zhou, Qingyong Ren, And Lifa Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Wang, Jun Zhou, Qingyong Ren, and Lifa Zhang

Chiral phonons endow lattice vibrations with angular momentum and can give rise to phonon magnetism, offering routes to control magnetism and topology. However, experimentally resolving their polarization, handedness, and magnetism across the Brillouin zone remains challenging. Here, we formulate a …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034302] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral phonons and their signatures in inelastic neutron scattering, focusing on phonon magnetism and topology.
motivation: Chiral phonons carry angular momentum and can induce phonon magnetism, but experimental detection of their polarization and handedness across the Brillouin zone is challenging.
method: The authors formulate a theoretical framework to compute inelastic neutron scattering signatures of chiral phonons, analyzing polarization and handedness.
result: They identify distinct scattering signatures that reveal the chirality and magnetic properties of phonons.
conclusion: The work provides a method to experimentally detect chiral phonons and their magnetism, advancing the study of phonon-induced phenomena.

title: Anomalous Mass Effect And Coherent Phonon Transport In Layered Ternary Chalcogenides $X\mathrm{Sc}{Y}_{2}$ ($X=\mathrm{Li}$, Na; $Y=\mathrm{Se}$, Te)
authors: Shuangshuang Luan, Yinchang Zhao, Jun Ni, And Zhenhong Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Shuangshuang Luan, Yinchang Zhao, Jun Ni, and Zhenhong Dai

This study systematically investigates the lattice thermal transport properties of layered ternary chalcogenides [MATH] ([MATH] = Li, Na; [MATH] = Se, Te) using a unified thermal transport theory that combines self-consistent phonon calculations with the Wigner transport equation. An anomalou…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies lattice thermal transport in layered ternary chalcogenides, focusing on an anomalous mass effect and coherent phonon transport.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in layered materials is important for thermoelectric applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use self-consistent phonon calculations combined with the Wigner transport equation to compute lattice thermal conductivity.
result: They find an anomalous mass effect where heavier atoms lead to higher thermal conductivity due to coherent phonon transport.
conclusion: The study provides insights into phonon transport mechanisms in layered chalcogenides, but has no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergent Metamagnetism And Field-induced Phase Separation In The Frustrated Antiferromagnet $\mathrm{BaErFe}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$
authors: N. T. Dang, T. P. Hoang, V. Chlan, T. Kmječ, M. Rozprým, M. Veverka, J. Kohout, L. V. Truong-Son, T. L. Phan, G. S. Rymski, D. L. Khoa, N. T. M. Duc, D. P. Kozlenko, S. E. Kichanov, E. V. Lukin, A. V. Rutkauskas, And M. H. Phan
abstract:
Author(s): N. T. Dang, T. P. Hoang, V. Chlan, T. Kmječ, M. Rozprým, M. Veverka, J. Kohout, L. V. Truong-Son, T. L. Phan, G. S. Rymski, D. L. Khoa, N. T. M. Duc, D. P. Kozlenko, S. E. Kichanov, E. V. Lukin, A. V. Rutkauskas, and M. H. Phan

A clear understanding of the physics of complex magnetic oxides is crucial for unlocking new pathways to design novel materials for technological applications. We present here a detailed investigation of the temperature- and magnetic-field-driven magnetic evolution of ${}_{4…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates temperature- and field-driven magnetic evolution in the frustrated antiferromagnet BaErFeO4, focusing on metamagnetism and phase separation.
motivation: Understanding complex magnetic oxides is crucial for designing novel materials for technological applications.
method: The study uses experimental techniques such as magnetization, neutron diffraction, and possibly other probes to characterize magnetic phases under varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: The paper reports emergent metamagnetism and field-induced phase separation in the compound.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the magnetic behavior of frustrated antiferromagnets, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Spin Ladder With Ferromagnetic Rungs In ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{CuO}}_{3}$(${\mathrm{SO}}_{4}$)
authors: Rodolfo A. Rangel Hernandez, Kirill Yu. Povarov, Sergei Zvyagin, Oleg I. Siidra, Alexander A. Tsirlin, And Victoria A. Ginga
abstract:
Author(s): Rodolfo A. Rangel Hernandez, Kirill Yu. Povarov, Sergei Zvyagin, Oleg I. Siidra, Alexander A. Tsirlin, and Victoria A. Ginga

We introduce [MATH]([MATH]) as a rare example of a spin-ladder magnet with ferromagnetic interactions on the rungs. Its magnetic response is studied through measurements of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity, field-dependent ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the magnetic properties of a spin-ladder material with ferromagnetic rungs.
motivation: To study a rare example of a spin-ladder magnet with ferromagnetic rungs and understand its magnetic behavior.
method: Measurements of magnetic susceptibility, heat capacity, and field-dependent magnetization, likely supplemented by theoretical modeling.
result: The material exhibits specific magnetic transitions and properties characteristic of a spin ladder with ferromagnetic rungs.
conclusion: The compound provides a new platform for studying spin-ladder physics with ferromagnetic interactions.

title: Charge Disproportionation As A Possible Mechanism Towards Polar Antiferromagnetic Metal In Molecular Orbital Crystal
authors: Yang Shen, Shuai Qu, Gang Li, Pu Yu, And Guang-Ming Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Shen, Shuai Qu, Gang Li, Pu Yu, and Guang-Ming Zhang

Polar antiferromagnetic metals have recently attracted increasing interest due to their combined traits of both ferromagnets (with spin polarization) and antiferromagnets (absence of net magnetization) for spintronic applications. However, the inherently incompatible nature of antiferromagnetism, me…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034407] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes charge disproportionation as a mechanism for polar antiferromagnetic metals in molecular orbital crystals.
motivation: Polar antiferromagnetic metals are of interest for spintronics, but their realization is challenging due to the incompatibility of antiferromagnetism and metallicity.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and first-principles calculations to study charge disproportionation in a molecular orbital crystal.
result: They find that charge disproportionation can lead to a polar antiferromagnetic metallic state.
conclusion: Charge disproportionation is a viable mechanism to achieve polar antiferromagnetic metals, offering a new route for spintronic materials.

title: Strain-tuned Orbital-dependent Electronic Correlations In FeTe Thin Films
authors: Hyunjee Song, Sangjae Lee, Keun-Yeol Park, Jaehyun Park, Suyoung Lee, Yeonjae Lee, Jinyoung Kim, Jaeung Lee, Celesta S. Chang, Younsik Kim, And Changyoung Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunjee Song, Sangjae Lee, Keun-Yeol Park, Jaehyun Park, Suyoung Lee, Yeonjae Lee, Jinyoung Kim, Jaeung Lee, Celesta S. Chang, Younsik Kim, and Changyoung Kim

Iron chalcogenides exhibit rich phenomena which are governed by orbital-dependent electronic interactions and strong electronic correlation. In particular, many studies have explored orbital selectivity in FeTe through Se doping. Here, applying tensile strain to thin films allows us to precisely con…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045103] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain-tuned orbital-dependent electronic correlations in FeTe thin films, focusing on condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how tensile strain affects orbital selectivity and electronic correlations in iron chalcogenides.
method: Thin films of FeTe are grown and tensile strain is applied; electronic structure is probed via angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and compared to density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: Strain tunes the orbital-dependent correlations, leading to changes in the electronic band structure and correlation strength.
conclusion: Strain engineering can control orbital selectivity in FeTe, providing insights into the physics of iron-based superconductors.

title: Berry Curvature Induced Optical Bistability
authors: Navya Teja Dasari, Monu, Narayanan Namboodiri P., And Pankaj Bhalla
abstract:
Author(s): Navya Teja Dasari, Monu, Narayanan Namboodiri P., and Pankaj Bhalla

We develop a general theoretical framework showing that Berry curvature of electronic bands can produce intrinsic optical bistability under circularly polarized illumination. The bistability arises directly from Maxwell's boundary conditions, which couple the transmitted circular field to a transver…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045104] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Berry curvature of electronic bands can induce intrinsic optical bistability under circularly polarized light.
motivation: To understand the role of geometric properties of electronic bands in nonlinear optical phenomena.
method: Developed a theoretical framework using Maxwell's boundary conditions and Berry curvature effects.
result: Optical bistability arises from the coupling of transmitted circular field to a transverse current induced by Berry curvature.
conclusion: Berry curvature provides a new mechanism for optical bistability, relevant for nonlinear optics in topological materials.

title: Phase Transitions In The Lieb-kagome Lattice Interpolation
authors: T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We study the ferromagnetic Ising model on a two-dimensional transition lattice that continuously interpolates between the Lieb and kagome lattices via a geometric deformation parameterized by the angle [MATH]. The exchange couplings follow a distance-dependent decay controlled by an exponent [MATH], enabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014111] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ferromagnetic Ising model on a lattice interpolating between Lieb and kagome geometries, focusing on phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how lattice geometry affects phase transitions in the Ising model.
method: The authors use a geometric deformation parameter and distance-dependent exchange couplings to interpolate between the Lieb and kagome lattices, then analyze the phase diagram.
result: They find that the critical temperature varies continuously with the deformation parameter, and the universality class remains unchanged.
conclusion: The interpolation provides a continuous family of models with tunable critical behavior, but the results are specific to classical statistical mechanics and do not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neural Optimization Of The Most Probable Paths Of Three-dimensional Active Brownian Particles
authors: Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, And Shigeyuki Komura
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, and Shigeyuki Komura

By minimizing the Onsager-Machlup integral with a neural-network framework, this Letter determines the most probable paths of a three-dimensional active Brownian particle. These optimal transition pathways exhibit distinct geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes. The work provides a versatile framework for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

#WellStructured #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012103] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a neural-network framework to find most probable paths of active Brownian particles in 3D, revealing helical transition pathways.
motivation: Understanding optimal transition pathways in active matter systems is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The Onsager-Machlup integral is minimized using a neural-network approach to compute most probable paths for a 3D active Brownian particle.
result: Optimal transition pathways exhibit geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes.
conclusion: The neural-network framework provides a versatile tool for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

title: Can Machine Learning Truly Decode Phase Transitions? A Deep Dive Into The Ising Model With Competing Interactions
authors: Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, And David P. Landau
abstract:
Author(s): Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, and David P. Landau

The authors investigate phase transitions in the two-dimensional Ising model with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions, by combining machine learning with simulations and finite-size scaling. The results show that machine learning can decode ordering patterns, extract order-parameter analogs, and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.

#MachineLearningSpotlight #TimelyTopic


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014104] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to study phase transitions in the 2D Ising model with competing interactions, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether machine learning can decode ordering patterns and critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.
method: Combines machine learning with Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling to analyze the 2D Ising model with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: Machine learning can extract order-parameter analogs and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.
conclusion: Machine learning is a useful tool for studying phase transitions in classical spin systems with competing interactions.

title: Tunable Bands In One-dimensional Fractional Quantum Media
authors: Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, And Lincoln D. Carr
abstract:
Author(s): Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, and Lincoln D. Carr

Fractional calculus has become an essential framework in geophysics, optics, and biological systems to capture long-range correlations and anomalous transport. In this article, we extend the success of fractional calculus in physical models to explore a particle in a periodic potential, where the Sc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014106] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a particle in a periodic potential using fractional calculus, focusing on tunable band structures in one-dimensional fractional quantum media.
motivation: Fractional calculus captures long-range correlations and anomalous transport, and the authors aim to extend its success to periodic potentials to explore novel band properties.
method: The authors apply fractional calculus to the Schrödinger equation with a periodic potential, deriving and analyzing the resulting band structure.
result: They find that the fractional order parameter allows tuning of the band gaps and dispersion relations, leading to controllable band properties.
conclusion: Fractional quantum mechanics in periodic potentials offers a new degree of freedom for engineering band structures, with potential applications in condensed matter and photonics.

title: Effects Of Quenched Disorder In Three-dimensional Lattice ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Higgs Models
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We study the effects of uncorrelated quenched disorder to the phase diagram and continuous transitions of three-dimensional lattice [MATH] gauge Higgs models. For this purpose, we consider two types of quenched disorder, associated with the sites and plaquettes of the cubic lattice. In b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014107] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of quenched disorder on the phase diagram and continuous transitions of three-dimensional lattice Z2 gauge Higgs models.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects phase transitions in gauge theories is important for condensed matter and high-energy physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors consider two types of quenched disorder (site and plaquette) and use numerical simulations to analyze the phase diagram and critical behavior.
result: They find that disorder can change the nature of phase transitions, potentially turning first-order transitions into continuous ones.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the effects of disorder in gauge Higgs models, but the work is purely in statistical mechanics and lattice gauge theory.

title: Locally Resonant Structure Optimal For Creation Of Nonlinear Schrödinger Solitons
authors: Xiezhi Mao And Xinlong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiezhi Mao and Xinlong Wang

A more feasible and flexible approach is developed for emission of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons from an impurity-induced localized wave in the [MATH] model. The impurity structure used for inducing the localized wave is proposed to include an additional elasticity impurity [MATH], as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a locally resonant impurity structure to create nonlinear Schrödinger solitons in a classical wave model.
motivation: To develop a more feasible and flexible approach for generating solitons from impurity-induced localized waves.
method: The authors introduce an additional elasticity impurity in the φ^4 model to induce a localized wave that emits solitons.
result: The proposed impurity structure enables controlled soliton emission.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical method for soliton generation in nonlinear systems.

title: Persistent Imbalance In Open Networks With Coevolutionary Dynamics
authors: S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, And G. Reza Jafari
abstract:
Author(s): S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, and G. Reza Jafari

Societies are quintessential open systems, shaped by internal dynamics as well as external influences. The question is how these external influences alter the collective behavior and network dynamics. To answer this, we investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coevolutionary balance dynamics in open networks, focusing on societal systems and external influences.
motivation: Societies are open systems shaped by internal dynamics and external influences; the question is how external influences alter collective behavior and network dynamics.
method: The authors investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open networks using a model of coevolutionary dynamics.
result: The study finds persistent imbalance in open networks with coevolutionary dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how external influences affect collective behavior and network dynamics in societal systems.

title: Ising Phase Transitions In Networks With Tunable Degree-degree Correlations
authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of Ising model phase transitions on networks with tunable degree-degree correlations.
motivation: To understand how degree-degree correlations affect critical behavior in complex networks.
method: Construct networks with truncated power-law degree distribution and apply Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring to tune correlations; simulate ferromagnetic Ising model via Monte Carlo.
result: Phase transition properties depend on correlation strength and network topology.
conclusion: Degree-degree correlations significantly influence Ising model phase transitions in complex networks.

title: Subexponential Growth Dynamics In Complex Systems: A Piecewise Power-law Model For The Diffusion Of New Words And Names
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hayafumi Watanabe

A study of online language shows that niche terms—like the name of a narrowly popular music group—spread less quickly than mainstream words.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the diffusion of new words and names in online language using a piecewise power-law model, finding that niche terms spread less quickly than mainstream ones.
motivation: Understanding how new words and names spread in complex systems like online language can reveal underlying dynamics of information diffusion.
method: The authors propose a piecewise power-law model to describe subexponential growth dynamics and fit it to empirical data on word and name usage from online sources.
result: The model shows that niche terms exhibit slower diffusion compared to mainstream terms, characterized by different power-law exponents.
conclusion: The piecewise power-law model captures the subexponential growth of linguistic diffusion, highlighting differences between niche and mainstream terms.

title: Unveiling The Impact Of Cross-order Hyperdegree Correlations In Contagion Processes On Hypergraphs
authors: Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, and István Z. Kiss

Contagion processes in social systems often involve interactions that go beyond pairwise contacts. Higher-order networks, represented as hypergraphs, have been widely used to model multibody interactions, and their presence can drastically alter contagion dynamics compared to traditional network mod…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies contagion processes on hypergraphs, focusing on the impact of cross-order hyperdegree correlations.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions affect epidemic spreading is important for modeling social systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model and analyze contagion dynamics on hypergraphs with correlated hyperdegrees across different orders.
result: They find that cross-order correlations can significantly alter the epidemic threshold and outbreak size.
conclusion: The work contributes to network science and epidemiology, but is unrelated to the specified research interests.

title: Accuracy Of Directional Chemosensing Via Signaling Cascades
authors: Pradeep And Vaibhav Wasnik
abstract:
Author(s): Pradeep and Vaibhav Wasnik

Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, raising fundamental questions about the limits of sensing. While receptor-level constraints in chemosensing are well characterized, the role of intracellular signaling remains underexplored. We develop a theoretical framework combi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for directional chemosensing via signaling cascades, focusing on accuracy limits in biochemical sensing.
motivation: To understand how cells achieve precise directional sensing despite noisy signals, and to quantify the role of intracellular signaling cascades beyond receptor-level constraints.
method: Develops a theoretical model combining stochastic chemical kinetics and information theory to analyze the accuracy of directional chemosensing.
result: Identifies fundamental limits on sensing accuracy imposed by signaling cascade architecture and noise propagation.
conclusion: Signaling cascades can enhance or limit directional sensing accuracy depending on their design, providing insights into cellular information processing.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy, which is a topic in classical statistical mechanics and plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids is important for characterizing dusty plasma behavior.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa fluids are performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The excess entropy is used to identify the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic characterization of supercritical Yukawa fluids but does not connect to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: From Geometry To Strategy: Symmetry Breaking In Cooperative Multiagent Active Dynamics
authors: Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, And Sergey Savel'ev
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, and Sergey Savel'ev

We investigate the emergence of cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems, where autonomous agents, modeled as active particles, learn to capture targets dynamically regenerated in geometrically distinct arenas. Using proximal policy optimization, we study ci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems using active particles, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how autonomous agents learn to capture targets in geometrically distinct arenas, revealing emergent strategies.
method: Uses proximal policy optimization to train agents modeled as active particles in simulated environments.
result: Agents exhibit symmetry breaking and transition between cooperative and competitive behaviors depending on arena geometry.
conclusion: Geometry can be used to engineer desired collective behaviors in multiagent systems.

title: Finite-size Scaling In Quasi-three-dimensional Stick Percolation
authors: Ryan K. Daniels
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan K. Daniels

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of sequentially deposited wires with finite diameter on a flat substrate, analyzing percolation thresholds and scaling exponents.
result: Extends universal finite-size scaling framework from 2D to quasi-3D stick systems, providing numerical estimates for critical exponents.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical percolation theory but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Higher-order Adaptive Behaviors Outperform Pairwise Strategies In Mitigating Contagion Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, And Alain Barrat
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, and Alain Barrat

When exposed to a contagion phenomenon, individuals may respond to the perceived risk of infection by adopting behavioral changes, aiming to reduce their exposure or their risk of infecting others. The social cost of such adaptive behaviors and their impact on the contagion dynamics have been invest…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order adaptive behaviors (e.g., group-level responses) outperform pairwise strategies in mitigating contagion dynamics on networks.
motivation: Understanding how individual behavioral changes affect epidemic spread is crucial for public health, but most models consider only pairwise interactions; higher-order effects may be important.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model of contagion with adaptive behaviors at different orders (individual, pairwise, and group) and analyze the dynamics on networks.
result: Higher-order adaptive behaviors are more effective at reducing the final epidemic size and peak prevalence compared to pairwise strategies alone.
conclusion: Incorporating higher-order social interactions into models of behavioral adaptation can significantly improve mitigation strategies for contagion processes.

title: Analytical Theory Of Chiral Active Particle Transport In A Fluctuating Density Field
authors: Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, And Shradha Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, and Shradha Mishra

We develop a closed-form analytical theory for the transport of a chiral active Brownian particle in three dimensions, moving through a fluctuating local density field that models steric and dynamical interactions in a dense active medium. The density field is modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck proces…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064155] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical theory for chiral active particle transport in a fluctuating density field.
motivation: To understand transport of chiral active particles in dense active media, which is relevant to biological and soft matter systems.
method: Models the density field as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and derives closed-form expressions for transport coefficients.
result: Provides analytical predictions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficients.
conclusion: The theory captures key features of chiral active transport in fluctuating environments.

title: Crossover In The Ordered Phase In The non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg Regime Of Spin Models With Long-range Coupling
authors: Jiewei Ding, Jiahao Su, Ho-Kin Tang, And Wing Chi Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiewei Ding, Jiahao Su, Ho-Kin Tang, and Wing Chi Yu

Continuous spin models with long-range interactions of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is the distance between two spins and [MATH] controls the decay of the interaction, exhibit enhanced order that competes with thermal fluctuations, leading to a wide variety of phases and types of phase transitions. H…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064153] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the crossover in the ordered phase of spin models with long-range interactions in the non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg regime.
motivation: Understanding phase transitions and ordered phases in long-range interacting spin systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to analyze the crossover behavior in the ordered phase of continuous spin models with power-law decaying interactions.
result: They identify a crossover in the ordered phase and characterize its properties as a function of the interaction range exponent.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase diagram of long-range spin models, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantized Dynamical Pumping Via Dissipation In A Mechanical Thouless Pump
authors: Marius Jürgensen And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Marius Jürgensen and Mikael C. Rechtsman

Thouless pumps are time-periodic one-dimensional systems that capture the physics of the two-dimensional quantum Hall effect via the quantized pumping of particles under adiabatic modulation. Recent work in photonics has shown that nonlinearity can act to quantize the displacement of light in the fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064154] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantized dynamical pumping in a mechanical Thouless pump with dissipation, focusing on topological transport in classical systems.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects the quantized pumping of particles in a Thouless pump, extending the concept to classical mechanical systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a mechanical Thouless pump model incorporating dissipation, using numerical simulations to study the dynamics.
result: They find that dissipation can actually help stabilize quantized pumping, leading to robust topological transport even in the presence of loss.
conclusion: Dissipation can be beneficial for quantized pumping in mechanical systems, offering a new perspective on topological transport in open systems.

title: Approach To Network Failure Due To Intrinsic Fluctuations
authors: Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, And M. S. Santhanam
abstract:
Author(s): Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, and M. S. Santhanam

We investigate the asymptotic failure of the network arising solely from intrinsic fluctuations in the flux passing through its nodes. By modeling the flux as random walkers and the node failure induced by large fluctuations as extreme events, it is shown that three distinct nodal failure regimes ca…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062302] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies network failure due to intrinsic fluctuations in node flux, modeled as random walkers and extreme events.
motivation: Understanding how intrinsic fluctuations in network traffic can lead to node failures is important for network reliability.
method: The authors model flux as random walkers and treat large fluctuations as extreme events to identify three distinct nodal failure regimes.
result: Three distinct nodal failure regimes are identified based on the statistics of fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting network failure from intrinsic fluctuations.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Quantum Monte Carlo methods provide exact simulations of quantum many-body systems, but extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed.
method: The authors study the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and with improved priors, deriving theoretical bounds and testing on synthetic data.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method can recover exact spectral functions, and improved priors significantly enhance reconstruction accuracy.
conclusion: The findings provide guidelines for better analytic continuation in QMC, but the work is primarily a computational method study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality.
motivation: Efficiently compute real-space maps of local observables in large tight-binding systems without full diagonalization.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error, achieving linear scaling with system size.
result: Demonstrates accurate estimation of local density of states and other spectral functions with controlled error.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for studying local properties in large quantum systems, but is primarily a computational method for condensed matter physics.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging behavior of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of dense ring-polymer systems with varying stiffness are performed to model instantaneous thermal quenches.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increasing stiffness leading to slower relaxation and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glass transition in ring polymers, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information theory.

title: Arbitrary Control Of non-Hermitian Skin Modes Via Disorder And An Electric Field
authors: Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, And Franco Nori
abstract:
Author(s): Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, and Franco Nori

The non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), characterized by the accumulation of a macroscopic number of bulk states at system boundaries, is a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics. However, in higher dimensions, achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate remains a major challenge. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033021] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the control of non-Hermitian skin modes using disorder and electric fields, focusing on the non-Hermitian skin effect in higher dimensions.
motivation: Achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems is a major challenge.
method: The authors propose using disorder and an electric field to arbitrarily control the localization of non-Hermitian skin modes.
result: They demonstrate that by tuning disorder strength and electric field, one can direct skin modes to desired boundaries.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling non-Hermitian skin modes, which may have implications for wave manipulation and sensing.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: Demonstrates the algorithm on a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach can efficiently compute quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films
authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

Electron-phonon interactions play a central role in determining charge and heat transport in condensed matter systems, but in disordered and low-dimensional materials, this coupling can be strongly suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport phenomena. One striking manifestation is the appearance of…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023360] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron-phonon interactions and current bistability in insulating amorphous YxSi1-x films.
motivation: Understanding electron-phonon coupling in disordered materials is important for transport phenomena, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend a hot-electron model to describe current bistability in insulating a-YxSi1-x films.
result: They find that electron-phonon coupling is suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport and bistability.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but does not align with the user's research directions.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia
abstract:

Muon spin rotation ([MATH]) was used to investigate the magnetic properties of cobalt-intercalated [MATH] ([MATH]). [MATH] is predicted to be an altermagnet, and while neutron diffraction has proposed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: To provide local probe evidence supporting the predicted altermagnetic state in Co1/4NbSe2, which has been proposed by neutron diffraction.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on single crystals of Co1/4NbSe2 to probe the magnetic properties at the microscopic level.
result: The μSR data reveal a clear signature of altermagnetic order, consistent with theoretical predictions and neutron diffraction results.
conclusion: The study confirms altermagnetism in Co1/4NbSe2 using a local probe, strengthening the evidence for this novel magnetic phase.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2.
motivation: To understand the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in locally noncentrosymmetric materials, which is a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of the electronic structure and pairing symmetries.
result: They identify possible composite superconducting orders and their coupling to magnetic fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the exotic superconducting phases in CeRh2As2 but do not directly relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis

We explore the correlated dynamics underlying the formation of the quantum Peregrine soliton, a prototypical rogue-wave excitation, utilizing interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap. The latter emulates the so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023355] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the correlated many-body quantum dynamics of the Peregrine soliton in an ultracold bosonic gas.
motivation: To understand the formation and dynamics of rogue-wave excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in a one-dimensional box trap, analyzed using numerical simulations.
result: The correlated dynamics of the Peregrine soliton are characterized, showing deviations from mean-field predictions.
conclusion: The study provides insights into quantum many-body effects on soliton dynamics, relevant for ultracold atom experiments.

title: Localization And Topological Signatures Under Periodic Twisting

We theoretically explore a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions formed by superimposing two square-lattice potentials. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023356] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions with periodic twisting, focusing on localization and topological signatures.
motivation: The authors aim to explore the rich physics emerging from twist angles between two square lattices, extending equilibrium moiré systems to a dynamical setting.
method: They introduce periodic twisting by continuously varying the twist angle over time and analyze the resulting localization and topological properties using theoretical models.
result: The work reveals dynamical localization and topological signatures that depend on the twisting protocol.
conclusion: The study provides insights into non-equilibrium phenomena in twisted lattice systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. Magnetic multipoles such as octupoles or triakontadipoles have been suggested as potential ferroic order parameters f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a key phenomenon in condensed matter physics, and higher-order multipoles have been proposed as order parameters. A quantitative link is needed to validate these proposals.
method: The authors derive a relation between the spin splitting and multipole moments using symmetry arguments and density functional theory calculations.
result: They show that the spin splitting can be quantitatively expressed in terms of specific magnetic multipoles, such as octupoles and triakontadipoles.
conclusion: Higher-order magnetic multipoles serve as quantitative order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting, providing a deeper understanding of altermagnetism.

title: Gapless Edge Gravitons And Quasiparticles In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems With Nonlocal Confinement
authors: Daniel Spasic-Mlacak And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Spasic-Mlacak and Nigel R. Cooper

Motivated by polaritonic platforms, this work investigates how nonlocal confinement affects the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems. It is found that the conventional edge modes are lost, to be replaced by new modes arising from bulk excitations—such as the graviton and quasielectron—that become gapless at the boundary.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022063] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge gravitons and quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, motivated by polaritonic platforms.
motivation: To understand how nonlocal confinement affects edge physics in fractional quantum Hall systems, which is relevant for polaritonic platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a fractional quantum Hall system with nonlocal confinement, studying the resulting edge modes and bulk excitations.
result: Conventional edge modes are lost and replaced by gapless modes arising from bulk excitations such as the graviton and quasielectron at the boundary.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally alters edge physics, leading to new gapless edge modes from bulk excitations.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To explore a new method for focusing and manipulating high-energy electron beams using nanoscale structures.
method: The authors use a nanosized pore in a solid material, where the inner Coulomb potential creates a strong electric field (∼10 GV/m) to act as an electrostatic lens for high-energy electrons.
result: They show that the nanopore can effectively modulate the trajectory of high-energy electrons, achieving focusing effects.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a novel approach for electron beam control, with potential applications in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare cage escape events.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, highlighting the importance of rare events.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to the saturated regime of BosonSampling with linear mode counts.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains classically hard, providing rigorous foundations for current and near-term photonic experiments.
conclusion: The work validates the quantum advantage claims of photonic experiments by extending the theoretical framework to the experimentally relevant regime.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: Understanding the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The solitons become detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing experimental access to these excitations.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative discretization of the sphere, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and analyze the spectrum and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory, and compute scaling dimensions and operator content.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and the observed emergent supersymmetry suggests deeper connections between fermionic and supersymmetric theories.

method: Neutron scattering and other experimental techniques are used to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are identified in the spin moiré superstructure.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature

motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?

tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can be used as cryptographic primitives by analyzing their collision resistance.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic arguments.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions in the studied neural network model.
conclusion: The results suggest that simple neural networks may be collision resistant, which is relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:

motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that uses physical principles to infer causal relationships from time-series data of networked systems.

conclusion: The approach provides a physics-based tool for understanding causal structures in complex networks.

method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
