tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the phase transition and ground state properties in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which may exhibit exotic magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the critical behavior and symmetry breaking.
result: The system undergoes a three-dimensional XY universality class transition, and the ground state shows hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic properties of kagome spin ice systems and the universality class of their phase transitions.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but typically require low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, with tunability via chemical composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at accessible temperatures, potentially enabling new quantum phenomena.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2 via attractive polaron spectroscopy.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy measurements on twisted bilayer WSe2, analyzing attractive polaron features to infer electronic and magnetic properties.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstration of electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 hosts a tunable quantum anomalous Hall state, relevant for topological quantum devices.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information through phase transitions.
motivation: Cells need to process complex environmental signals, and phase transitions offer a potential mechanism for computation.
method: The paper provides a conceptual framework linking phase separation to information processing, drawing on analogies from physics and biology.
result: It suggests that phase transitions enable cells to classify and respond to multiple signals simultaneously.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation may be a powerful computational strategy in biology, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing and electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control and spin-dependent electron optics in graphene for spintronic applications.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control via spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for spin control in graphene, advancing spintronics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state is key to their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify and describe the dipolar nematic ordering in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The nematic ordering underpins relaxor ferroelectric behavior, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, meaning domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that the thermodynamic limit is universal and independent of boundary conditions or domain shape in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries and analyze the ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit is not always well-defined in certain quantum spin and dimer models, which has implications for our understanding of phase transitions and quantum order.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the non-equilibrium dynamics and hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations.
result: Discovery of a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present at equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable states with distinct properties, offering a route to control correlated materials.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams with provable exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, as proven theoretically.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, though it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each with specific milestones, based on their expertise in quantum computing.
result: A five-stage roadmap for quantum computing development is presented.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level guide for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on achieving practical quantum advantage.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding magnetic phenomena in 2D materials and their potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling forces.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view using space-time duality.
method: The review focuses on discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified framework for understanding dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy that simplifies the analysis of interacting many-body dynamics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematic states.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theory.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories provide a powerful framework for analyzing these systems, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are useful for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various fields, but the paper is pedagogical and not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and simulation studies of spin-glass dynamics.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with ongoing experimental and theoretical developments, offering insights into frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity in the brain.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity to enable perception, thought, and action is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover reproducible behaviors in neural data and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can achieve predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on their integration into practical applications.
conclusion: The paper concludes that theoretical models of internal conversion can be effectively applied to photonics and energy harvesting, but does not present novel results or deep connections to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel quantum technologies, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the standard model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and reviews experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson couplings and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions behind the bounds, and that materials can be engineered to circumvent these assumptions.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds enables the design of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits, without violating thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A review of synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on topological and gravitational analogies.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, discussing lattice geometries, curvature, and dimensionality.
result: It highlights progress in realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions, and their potential for simulating exotic physics.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries offers a versatile platform for studying topological phases and gravitational analogs, but remains largely exploratory.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment between orientation and velocity leads to novel active matter phenomena.
method: Unified mathematical and conceptual framework, review of existing models.
result: Self-alignment enables orbiting, synchronized motion, and other collective behaviors.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and matter-wave interferometry.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature and its interplay with quantum mechanics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement mediation by gravity) and experimental approaches (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: The review summarizes current experimental progress and theoretical predictions regarding gravity-induced decoherence, collapse of wavefunctions, and gravity-mediated entanglement.
conclusion: Experiments with massive quantum systems are poised to guide the theoretical description of gravity on a laboratory scale, potentially revealing quantum aspects of gravity.

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, and Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Ultrahigh-quality-factor (high-[MATH]) resonances are critical for spectrally selective applications such as label-free biosensing, low-threshold lasing, and quantum information process…

tldr: This paper studies high-quality-factor nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices for enhancing light-matter interactions.
motivation: Ultrahigh-Q resonances are critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing, but achieving them in plasmonic lattices is challenging.
method: The authors propose a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice design that supports nonlocal resonances with high Q-factors, analyzed via numerical simulations and theoretical modeling.
result: They demonstrate nonlocal resonances with Q-factors exceeding 10^4, significantly higher than conventional plasmonic lattices.
conclusion: Mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices provide a platform for ultrahigh-Q resonances, potentially useful for nanophotonic devices and quantum information processing.

title: Barium Autoionization For Efficient Ion Trap Loading
authors: Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, And Wesley C. Campbell

We report a theoretical and experimental investigation of autoionizing resonances from the [MATH] manifold in neutral barium for efficient loading of ion traps. Our calculations predict large resonant cross sections for many narrow autoionizing reson…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates autoionizing resonances in barium for efficient ion trap loading, focusing on atomic physics and laser spectroscopy.
motivation: Efficient loading of ion traps is crucial for quantum computing and sensing, but current methods are inefficient; this work aims to improve loading rates using autoionization.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of autoionizing resonance cross sections with experimental measurements in a barium atomic beam.
result: They identify several narrow autoionizing resonances with large cross sections that enable more efficient photoionization for trap loading.
conclusion: The proposed autoionization scheme can significantly enhance ion trap loading efficiency, benefiting trapped-ion quantum platforms.

title: Effective Theory Of Surface Oscillations In Self-bound Superfluid Droplets
authors: Jun Mitsuhashi, Keisuke Fujii, And Masaru Hongo
abstract:

We investigate the low-energy dynamics of small-amplitude surface oscillations of spherical superfluid droplets in vacuum. Starting from the effective field theory of superfluid phonons, we derive an effective action governing the surface oscillations under a fixed particle-number constraint. The no…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an effective field theory for surface oscillations of superfluid droplets, focusing on low-energy dynamics under fixed particle number.
motivation: To understand the low-energy dynamics of surface oscillations in self-bound superfluid droplets, which are relevant for quantum droplets and ultracold atomic systems.
method: Starting from an effective field theory of superfluid phonons, the authors derive an effective action for surface oscillations using a fixed particle-number constraint and a gradient expansion.
result: They obtain a dispersion relation for surface modes and show that the effective theory reproduces known results for capillary waves and can be extended to include higher-order corrections.
conclusion: The effective theory provides a systematic framework to study surface oscillations in superfluid droplets, with potential applications to quantum droplets and other self-bound systems.

title: Study Of The Boson Peak In Amorphous Ge-Sb-Te Using Machine Learning Potentials
authors: Pyungjin Park And Seung-Hoon Jhi
abstract:

An excess of low-frequency vibrational states beyond the Debye prediction—known as the boson peak—is a universal feature of disordered materials, yet its microscopic origin and connection to atomic-scale structural disorder remain unresolved. Here we study the microscopic origin and real time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the boson peak in amorphous Ge-Sb-Te using machine learning potentials, focusing on vibrational anomalies in disordered materials.
motivation: The boson peak is a universal feature of disordered materials whose microscopic origin remains unresolved; understanding it is important for material science.
method: Machine learning potentials are used to simulate atomic-scale structural disorder and compute vibrational density of states in amorphous Ge-Sb-Te.
result: The study identifies structural origins of the boson peak and tracks its real-time evolution.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the boson peak but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Promising Thermoelectric Properties Of Quasi-one-dimensional Phosphorus-based Materials By Tuning The Chainlike Twisting
authors: Jiang-Jiang Ma, Dan Zhang, Rong-Rong Ma, Changsheng Min, Zhihong Yuan, Xiao-Xiao Zhang, Peng-Fei Liu, Yu Zhou, Jingyu Li, And Wen Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Jiang-Jiang Ma, Dan Zhang, Rong-Rong Ma, Changsheng Min, Zhihong Yuan, Xiao-xiao Zhang, Peng-Fei Liu, Yu Zhou, Jingyu Li, and Wen Yin

The search for high-performance thermoelectrics is increasingly focused on quasi-one-dimensional (Q-1D) materials, which leverage quantum confinement effects to intrinsically decouple transport properties. Herein we report a series of Q-1D phosphidosilicates with systematically tunable structural di…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermoelectric properties of quasi-one-dimensional phosphorus-based materials by tuning chainlike twisting.
motivation: To find high-performance thermoelectrics using quasi-one-dimensional materials that leverage quantum confinement effects.
method: First-principles calculations and Boltzmann transport theory to compute electronic and thermal transport properties.
result: The materials show promising thermoelectric figures of merit due to low lattice thermal conductivity and high power factor.
conclusion: Tuning structural distortion in quasi-one-dimensional phosphidosilicates is an effective strategy for enhancing thermoelectric performance.

title: Asymmetric Reversal And Quantized Helical Modes In Ultrathin Magnetic Nanotubes With Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies asymmetric reversal and quantized helical modes in ultrathin magnetic nanotubes with interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, focusing on curvilinear nanomagnetism.
motivation: To understand the effects of curvature and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction on magnetization reversal and spin wave modes in 3D nanomagnetic structures.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations and analytical modeling to analyze the reversal process and helical modes in nanotubes.
result: They find asymmetric reversal behavior and quantized helical modes due to curvature-induced effects and interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of curvilinear nanomagnetism but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems. We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in a stochastic Van der Pol oscillator model for thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory observations is needed.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory data.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for analyzing thermoacoustic instabilities using stochastic oscillator models.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, studying how spatial embedding affects spreading processes.
motivation: Many real temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, yet standard activity-driven models ignore spatial aspects. The authors aim to develop a tractable model that captures both temporal and spatial heterogeneity.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven network model where nodes are placed in a metric space and move according to a random walk, with interactions occurring when nodes are within a certain distance. They derive analytical expressions for the percolation threshold and spreading dynamics using generating functions and mean-field approximations.
result: The model reveals that spatial constraints can significantly alter the spreading dynamics compared to the non-spatial activity-driven model, with a critical spatial scale that separates localized from global spreading. Analytical predictions are validated by simulations.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal activity-driven networks provide a more realistic yet analytically tractable framework for studying spreading processes in systems where both time-varying connectivity and spatial embedding are important.

title: Random Motility Regulation As A Generic Mechanism Of Community Formation
authors: Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, and Julien Tailleur

The self-organization of microbial ecosystems involves a large variety of mechanisms, ranging from biochemical signaling to population dynamics. Among these, the role of motility regulation has been little studied, despite the importance of active migration processes. Here we show how weak, random m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random motility regulation in microbial communities leads to self-organized pattern formation.
motivation: Understanding the role of motility regulation in microbial ecosystem self-organization is important but has been little studied.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of active particles with random motility switching and analyze its collective behavior.
result: Weak, random motility regulation can drive community formation and spatial structure.
conclusion: Random motility regulation is a generic mechanism for microbial community formation.

title: Complete Local Expansion Of The Availability Function In Random Sequential Adsorption Of Aligned Squares At Low Density: Termination At Fourth Order

At low coverage, the reduction of available space can be …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014110] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the low-density expansion of the availability function in random sequential adsorption of aligned squares, a problem in statistical mechanics.
motivation: Understanding the kinetics of irreversible deposition processes is important for modeling physical phenomena such as protein adsorption or colloidal deposition.
method: The authors derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function up to fourth order in coverage using combinatorial enumeration of configurations.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the coefficients up to fourth order, showing how the available area decreases with coverage.
conclusion: The work provides a precise characterization of the RSA process for aligned squares at low density, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mechanical Control Of The Height Distribution Of Adsorbed Viral Capsids
authors: Yeraldinne Carrasco Salas, Kassandra Gérard, Lauriane Lecoq, Anna Salvetti, Fabien Montel, Cendrine Faivre-Moskalenko, And Martin Castelnovo

The height of viral particles adsorbed on solid substrates is governed by the equilibrium between adhesion energy and capsid elasticity. tldr: This paper studies the mechanical control of height distribution of adsorbed viral capsids, focusing on viral stiffness and adhesion.
motivation: To understand the physical origin of broadening in the height distribution of viral particles on solid substrates, which serves as a proxy for viral stiffness.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and experimental measurements to analyze how mechanical forces affect the height distribution of viral capsids.
result: They find that the height distribution is governed by the balance between adhesion energy and capsid elasticity, and mechanical control can tune this distribution.
conclusion: The work provides insights into viral mechanics and offers a noninvasive method to probe viral stiffness, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonclassical Interfacial Response In Ionic Liquids At Blocking Electrodes

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.

motivation: Understanding the nonclassical interfacial response of ionic liquids is important for applications in energy storage and electrochemistry.
method: The authors analyze a symmetric binary ionic liquid model using linear response theory and compare two interfacial boundary conditions (Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev and another).
result: They find that electrostatic correlations significantly affect the differential capacitance and charge distribution near the electrodes.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition is crucial for accurately modeling ionic liquid behavior at blocking electrodes.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) affects collective states in adaptive oscillator networks with Hebbian coupling.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration strength.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective dynamical states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant for understanding synchronization in complex systems.

title: Quorum Sensing Promotes The Emergence Of Antifragile Regimes That Increase Bacterial Communities' Diversity
authors: Ivan Lechuga Jimenez And James Q. Boedicker

method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and their effect on diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can enhance community resilience and diversity through antifragile dynamics.

result: Revealed the structural confinement and thermal transport mechanisms in Schwarz crystals.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the stability and thermal properties of this novel solid state.

title: Engineering Magnetotransport Through Hierarchical Symmetry In Weyl Semimetal Superlattices
authors: Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, And Bernd Gotsmann

motivation: To explore how periodic potentials in 3D materials can tune electrical transport properties via hierarchical symmetry.
method: The authors engineer superlattices in Weyl semimetals and measure magnetotransport, analyzing the role of symmetry in scattering.
result: They demonstrate controllable modification of magnetotransport through superlattice engineering.
conclusion: Superlattice engineering in 3D materials offers a new route to tailor electronic properties, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang

Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…

motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors analyze adversarial attacks on neural network surrogates for CFD and evaluate their impact on prediction accuracy.
result: The surrogates are found to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, which can cause significant errors in predicted flow fields.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness should be considered when deploying ML surrogates in CFD applications.

title: Hydrodynamic Attraction And Hindered Diffusion Govern First-passage Times Of Swimming Microorganisms
authors: Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, And Christina Kurzthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, and Christina Kurzthaler

Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall reveal how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion shape first-passage-time statistics. The results show that wall-induced hindered diffusion can strongly delay wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction produces distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022060] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how microorganisms navigate near surfaces is important for biological and ecological processes, but the role of hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion on first-passage times is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion significantly affect the first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near walls, with implications for microbial ecology and biophysics.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:
Author(s): Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, and Oleg Kogan

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging in a two-dimensional swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.

title: Redirecting Countermoving Swarms Through Collision

result: They identify conditions under which collisions lead to redirection and characterize the resulting spatiotemporal patterns.
conclusion: Collisions can be exploited to redirect swarms, offering a potential control mechanism for multiswarm systems.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka

method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.

motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to investigate the liquid-vapor critical point of a model hyperuniform fluid.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
