title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on glass stability and boson peak.
motivation: Understanding the relationship between glass stability and low-frequency vibrational properties is important for materials science but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure vibrational density of states in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The study clarifies how glass stability affects the boson peak and low-frequency vibrations.
conclusion: The findings advance understanding of glass physics but are not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Gravitational Scattering Of Solitonic Boson Stars: Analytics Vs Numerics
authors: Thibault Damour, Tamanna Jain, And Ulrich Sperhake
abstract:
Author(s): Thibault Damour, Tamanna Jain, and Ulrich Sperhake

We study the scattering of two boson stars by comparing four sequences (at fixed energy and varying impact parameter) of numerical relativity simulations to an effective-one-body analytic description, taking into account both gravitational effects (point-mass and tidal) and short-range scalar-field …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gravitational scattering of boson stars using numerical relativity and an effective-one-body analytic model.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of compact objects beyond black holes and test analytic approximations against full numerical simulations.
method: Comparison of four sequences of numerical relativity simulations with an effective-one-body description including gravitational and scalar-field effects.
result: The analytic model shows good agreement with numerics for certain impact parameters but deviations at close encounters.
conclusion: The effective-one-body approach can describe boson star scattering, but further refinements are needed for strong-field regimes.

title: Reference Quadrupole Moments Of Transition Elements From Lamb Shifts In Muonic Atoms
authors: S. Rathi, K. von Schoeler, P. Indelicato, And B. Ohayon
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rathi, K. von Schoeler, P. Indelicato, and B. Ohayon

We present a novel method for accurately measuring the absolute electric quadrupole moments of light transition elements [MATH]. Our approach is based on performing precision muonic x-ray spectroscopy of the [MATH] manifold, which is also referred to as the Lamb shift. These transitions are to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023001] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to measure electric quadrupole moments of transition elements using muonic x-ray spectroscopy.
motivation: Accurate nuclear quadrupole moments are needed for understanding nuclear structure and testing atomic theory, but are difficult to measure for light transition elements.
method: The authors perform precision spectroscopy of the muonic Lamb shift (2p-2s transitions) in muonic atoms of transition elements, extracting the quadrupole moment from the hyperfine splitting.
result: They report improved absolute quadrupole moments for several isotopes, with uncertainties reduced compared to previous methods.
conclusion: Muonic x-ray spectroscopy provides a reliable and precise way to determine nuclear quadrupole moments for light transition elements.

title: Direct Observation Of Structural Disorder Near Critical Point In ${\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$ Crystal
authors: Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, And Lin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, and Lin Zhou

Critical points (CPs) in ferroelectrics are known for their association with giant dielectric and electromechanical responses, yet their structural origin, especially in nonrelaxor systems, remains unclear. We combine in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-bas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural disorder near the critical point in BaTiO3 using in situ TEM and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the structural origin of giant dielectric and electromechanical responses at critical points in ferroelectrics.
method: Combines in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-based simulations.
result: Direct observation of structural disorder near the critical point.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the microscopic mechanisms underlying enhanced responses at critical points.

title: Ab Initio Free-Energy Surfaces For Coupled Ion-Electron Transfer
authors: Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, And Troy van Voorhis
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, and Troy Van Voorhis

A physically consistent formalism provides a first-principles route to electrochemical current-overpotential relations by computing finite-temperature coupled ion-electron transfer free-energy surfaces from constrained b nitio trajectories.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a first-principles method to compute free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer in electrochemical systems.
motivation: Understanding coupled ion-electron transfer is crucial for modeling electrochemical reactions, but existing methods lack a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: The authors use constrained ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories to compute finite-temperature free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer.
result: They obtain physically consistent free-energy surfaces that yield current-overpotential relations from first principles.
conclusion: The formalism provides a route to first-principles electrochemical kinetics, bridging atomistic simulations and macroscopic electrochemistry.

title: Extended Mean-Field Theories For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, and William Bialek

An extended version of mean-field theory accurately captures activity patterns seen in networks of biological neurons.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018401] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops extended mean-field theories to model activity patterns in networks of biological neurons.
motivation: Understanding collective activity in neural networks is important for neuroscience, but standard mean-field approximations may miss higher-order correlations.
method: The authors propose an extended mean-field theory that incorporates corrections beyond the standard approach, likely using techniques from statistical physics.
result: The extended theory accurately captures activity patterns observed in real neuronal networks, outperforming standard mean-field predictions.
conclusion: Extended mean-field theories provide a more accurate framework for modeling biological neural networks, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Multifaceted Decay Of $^{116}\mathrm{Cs}$
authors: J. Dey, U. Datta, O. Tengblad, P. Das, A. Rahaman, B. K. Agrawal, S. Chakraborty, A. Gottberg, M. Kowalska, K. Mahata, S. Mandal, M. Madurga, E. Nacher, E. Rapisarda, N. Warr, W. Sengupta, C. Sharma, And T. Stora
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dey, U. Datta, O. Tengblad, P. Das, A. Rahaman, B. K. Agrawal, S. Chakraborty, A. Gottberg, M. Kowalska, K. Mahata, S. Mandal, M. Madurga, E. Nacher, E. Rapisarda, N. Warr, W. Sengupta, C. Sharma, and T. Stora

The multifaceted decay properties of [MATH] near the proton drip line have been studied at ISOLDE, CERN. More than six new unbound states of [MATH] have been identified. A novel phenomenon of low energy isoscalar octupole resonance has been observed. After proton decay, tha…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 012501] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decay properties of 116Cs near the proton drip line, identifying new unbound states and observing low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance.
motivation: To understand the multifaceted decay of 116Cs and explore nuclear structure near the proton drip line.
method: Experimental study at ISOLDE, CERN, using proton decay and gamma-ray spectroscopy.
result: More than six new unbound states of 116Cs were identified, and a low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance was observed.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into nuclear structure and decay modes near the proton drip line.

title: Real-Space Dynamic Electron Correlation In Beryllium
authors: Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, And Takeshi Egami
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, and Takeshi Egami

The size of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium is about 2 Å, but it extends up to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, demonstrating that electron correlations are affected significantly by electron dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the size and dynamics of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding electron correlation in real space is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor and reconstruct the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy, extending to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, showing significant dynamic effects.
conclusion: Electron correlations are significantly affected by electron dynamics, but the work is purely a condensed matter physics study without relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ab Initio Calculations Of The Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{Ac}}^{+}$
authors: Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, And Anastasia Borschevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, and Anastasia Borschevsky

Accurate spectroscopic investigations of the heaviest elements are inherently challenging, due to their short lifetimes and low production yields. Success of such measurements requires both dedicated experimental techniques and strong theoretical support. Laser resonance chromatography (LRC) is a pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012801] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio calculations of the electronic structure of Ac+ to support laser resonance chromatography experiments.
motivation: Accurate spectroscopic data for heavy elements like actinium are needed to interpret experimental measurements, but are difficult to obtain due to short lifetimes and low production yields.
method: Multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock (MCDHF) and relativistic configuration interaction (RCI) methods are used to compute energy levels, transition probabilities, and hyperfine constants.
result: The calculations provide predicted spectra and hyperfine structure for Ac+, aiding in the identification of spectral lines in laser resonance chromatography.
conclusion: The theoretical predictions will facilitate future experimental studies of Ac+ and contribute to understanding the electronic structure of heavy elements.

title: Strain Engineering Of Dielectric Properties And Phase Transitions In Orthorhombic $\mathrm{Hf}{\mathrm{O}}_{2}$
authors: Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, And Wei Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, and Wei Ren

Hafnium dioxide ([MATH]), commonly known as hafnia, serves as a critical high-[MATH] gate dielectric material in complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) devices and is also widely utilized in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) capacitors. To gain better understanding of t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain engineering of dielectric properties and phase transitions in orthorhombic HfO2 for CMOS and DRAM applications.
motivation: Hafnia is a critical high-k dielectric in CMOS and DRAM, and understanding its dielectric properties under strain is important for device performance.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) are used to investigate the effect of biaxial strain on the dielectric constant and phase stability of orthorhombic HfO2.
result: Strain can significantly modify the dielectric constant and induce phase transitions between different orthorhombic phases.
conclusion: Strain engineering is an effective way to tune the dielectric properties of HfO2 for improved performance in electronic devices.

title: Photoinduced Strain And Polarization Switching In Barium Titanate In The Far-infrared Spectral Range
authors: Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, And Andrei Kirilyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, and Andrei Kirilyuk

Short midinfrared laser pulses efficiently facilitate ultrafast manipulation of ferroic order parameters, including the full reversal of magnetization or ferroelectric polarization, with the invoked mechanisms relating to the properties of polar phonons in ionic crystals. Much less is known, however…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates photoinduced strain and polarization switching in barium titanate using far-infrared laser pulses.
motivation: Understanding ultrafast manipulation of ferroelectric order parameters is important for potential applications in data storage and optoelectronics.
method: The authors use short midinfrared laser pulses to excite polar phonons in barium titanate and measure the resulting strain and polarization changes.
result: They observe efficient photoinduced strain and polarization switching in the far-infrared spectral range.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate a mechanism for ultrafast control of ferroelectric properties, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superconductivity Of non-A15 Compounds In V-Sn Binary System
authors: Xin Li, Guo-Yong Shi, Rui-Tong Xiao, Zhi-Zhuo Liu, Hong Jiang, Yue-Hua Su, Huai-Jun Sun, Cai-Zhuang Wang, And Chao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Li, Guo-Yong Shi, Rui-Tong Xiao, Zhi-Zhuo Liu, Hong Jiang, Yue-Hua Su, Huai-Jun Sun, Cai-Zhuang Wang, and Chao Zhang

By combining a genetic algorithm for crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations, both thermodynamically stable and metastable phases in the V-Sn binary system are systematically investigated. The experimentally synthesized A15-type [MATH] and ${…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates thermodynamically stable and metastable phases in the V-Sn binary system using crystal structure prediction and first-principles calculations, focusing on superconductivity of non-A15 compounds.
motivation: To explore new superconducting phases beyond the known A15-type compounds in the V-Sn system.
method: Combined genetic algorithm for crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations to systematically search for stable and metastable phases.
result: Identified several thermodynamically stable and metastable phases, including non-A15 compounds with potential superconductivity.
conclusion: The V-Sn binary system hosts a variety of superconducting phases beyond A15, warranting further experimental investigation.

title: Devil's Staircase Magnetic Spirals In $\mathrm{N}{\mathrm{i}}_{2−x}\mathrm{C}{\mathrm{o}}_{x}\mathrm{ScSb}{\mathrm{O}}_{6}$
authors: Kunlang Ji, Elena Solana-Madruga, Angel M. Arevalo-Lopez, Pascal Manuel, And J. Paul Attfield
abstract:
Author(s): Kunlang Ji, Elena Solana-Madruga, Angel M. Arevalo-Lopez, Pascal Manuel, and J. Paul Attfield

[MATH] solid solutions ([MATH], 0.2, 0.3, 0.4) have been studied by magnetization and neutron powder diffraction measurements. All samples are magnetically ordered below ${T}_{}≈63{0ex}}\m…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034403] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic spirals in Ni2-xCoxScSbO6 solid solutions using magnetization and neutron diffraction.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ordering and spiral structures in these materials.
method: Magnetization measurements and neutron powder diffraction were performed on samples with varying Co concentration.
result: All samples exhibit magnetic order below ~63 K with devil's staircase magnetic spirals.
conclusion: The magnetic properties are characterized by complex spiral ordering, but no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is made.

title: Switching Magnetic Spin States Using Small Magnetic Fields In Compositionally Complex $\mathrm{Sm}(\mathrm{Ti},\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Mn},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni},\mathrm{Cu}){\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: R. K. Dokala, M. Geers, P. Nordblad, R. Clulow, And R. Mathieu
abstract:
Author(s): R. K. Dokala, M. Geers, P. Nordblad, R. Clulow, and R. Mathieu

High-entropy perovskites offer a unique platform for exploring magnetic phenomena arising from extreme [MATH]-site chemical disorder. In [MATH], where there are seven cations in equal amounts at the [MATH] site ([MATH], Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), we observe long-range ant…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034404] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic spin state switching in a high-entropy perovskite oxide using small magnetic fields.
motivation: High-entropy perovskites offer a platform to explore magnetic phenomena from extreme chemical disorder, and understanding spin state switching could lead to novel magnetic materials.
method: The authors synthesize a compositionally complex perovskite with seven cations at the B-site and characterize its magnetic properties using magnetometry and other techniques.
result: They observe long-range antiferromagnetic order and demonstrate that small magnetic fields can switch the magnetic spin states.
conclusion: The findings highlight the potential of high-entropy perovskites for magnetic applications, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Manifestation Of Asymmetric Manganite-ruthenate Interfaces
authors: Haoming Ling, Xin Du, Zhixiong Deng, Kai Hu, Qiangtao Sui, Zixin Fan, Lingyuan Kong, Dingyi Li, Shaojie Tai, Wei Li, Yan Liang, Pan Chen, Kai Liu, Zhaoliang Liao, Meng Meng, Xiaoran Liu, Zhen Wang, And Jiandi Zhang

Interfacial magnetism in complex oxide heterostructures underlies both fundamental many-body physics and advanced spintronic applications. Here we report a pronounced stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling in ${}_{0.78}{}_{0.22}{}_{3}/\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034409] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling in manganite-ruthenate heterostructures, focusing on interfacial magnetism in complex oxides.
motivation: Understanding interfacial magnetism in complex oxide heterostructures is important for fundamental many-body physics and spintronic applications.
method: The authors fabricated asymmetric manganite-ruthenate interfaces and characterized their magnetic properties using experimental techniques.
result: A pronounced stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling was observed in the heterostructures.
conclusion: The stacking order significantly influences interfacial magnetic coupling, which has implications for spintronic devices.

We report the growth and physical properties of single-crystalline [MATH] crystallizing in the [MATH] space group, which comprises alternating Ta-S layers and Bi layers with each Bi atom connected to adjacent S atoms. Temperatur…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the growth and hydrostatic pressure study of a single-crystal type-II superconductor Bi2Ta3S6.
motivation: To investigate the physical properties and pressure response of a new superconductor.
method: Single-crystal growth and hydrostatic pressure measurements.
result: Characterization of superconducting properties under pressure.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the superconducting behavior of Bi2Ta3S6.

title: Interaction Between Cell Membranes And Protein Inclusions In The Large-deformation Regime
authors: Gaetano Ferraro And Michele Castellana
abstract:
Author(s): Gaetano Ferraro and Michele Castellana

Biological membranes are dynamic surfaces whose shape and function are critically influenced by protein inclusions (PIs). While membrane deformations induced by PIs have been extensively studied in the small-deformation regime, a variety of processes involve strong membrane deformations. We investig…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction between cell membranes and protein inclusions under large deformations using a theoretical model.
motivation: Understanding how protein inclusions deform cell membranes is important for biological processes, but the large-deformation regime is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on continuum elasticity to describe membrane-protein interactions in the large-deformation regime.
result: The model predicts specific deformation patterns and energy landscapes for protein inclusions in membranes under large strains.
conclusion: The work provides insights into membrane mechanics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Effects Of Spatial Beam Coherence And Plasma Scale Length On Stimulated Raman Scattering And Two-plasmon Decay
authors: Chiharu Nakatsuji, Yuji Takagi, Gabriele Cristoforetti, Sota Matsuura, Takuya Honda, Daisuke Tanaka, Dimitri Batani, Takumi Sato, Shun Horimoto, Hideo Nagatomo, Yasuhiko Sentoku, Philippe D. Author(s): Chiharu Nakatsuji, Yuji Takagi, Gabriele Cristoforetti, Sota Matsuura, Takuya Honda, Daisuke Tanaka, Dimitri Batani, Takumi Sato, Shun Horimoto, Hideo Nagatomo, Yasuhiko Sentoku, Philippe D. Nicolaï, Kai Taketoshi, Naoki Yamagata, Norimasa Ozaki, Yasunobu Arikawa, Akifumi Yogo, Shinsuke Fujioka, and Keisuke Shigemori

We present an experimental investigation demonstrating that the suppression of parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions under conditions relevant to direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, specifically backward stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) and two-plasmon decay (TPD), shows the e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates the suppression of stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay in laser-plasma interactions relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions can degrade the performance of direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, so understanding how to suppress them is important.
method: The authors performed experiments varying spatial beam coherence and plasma scale length, measuring the resulting levels of backward stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay.
result: They found that increasing spatial beam coherence and adjusting plasma scale length can suppress these instabilities.
conclusion: Controlling beam coherence and plasma scale length is an effective strategy to mitigate parametric instabilities in inertial confinement fusion.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Djamel Benredjem And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Djamel Benredjem and Jean-Christophe Pain

The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict plasma opacity under stellar conditions for iron and nickel.
motivation: Accurate opacity predictions are crucial for understanding stellar interiors and spectra, but calculations under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive.
method: A deep learning model is trained on existing opacity data to predict spectral opacities for iron and nickel plasmas.
result: The deep learning approach achieves accurate opacity predictions with significantly reduced computational cost compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: Deep learning offers a practical tool for opacity calculations in astrophysical plasmas, enabling faster simulations of stellar conditions.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biomolecular condensates near membranes.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that surface phase separation is significantly altered by confinement, with implications for cellular organization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how surfaces and confinement influence phase behavior in biological systems.

title: Transition To Dilatation-dominated Isothermal Compressible Turbulence
authors: Shadab Alam, Christoph Federrath, And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Shadab Alam, Christoph Federrath, and Jörg Schumacher

The kinetic energy dissipation rate is of central importance for small-scale statistics in turbulent flows. Here, we report a transition to the dilatation-dominated regime of three-dimensional isothermal fully compressible, homogeneous, isotropic turbulence by moments of energy dissipation and its c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033011] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition to dilatation-dominated regime in isothermal compressible turbulence, focusing on kinetic energy dissipation statistics.
motivation: Understanding the small-scale statistics of turbulent flows is important for many physical systems, but this work is purely classical fluid dynamics.
method: Direct numerical simulations of three-dimensional isothermal compressible homogeneous isotropic turbulence are performed, analyzing moments of energy dissipation and its components.
result: A transition to a dilatation-dominated regime is identified based on the scaling of dissipation moments.
conclusion: The findings characterize a regime change in compressible turbulence but have no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Shear Jamming Transition In Alternating Shear Rotation For Frictional And Frictionless Suspensions
authors: Pappu Acharya And Martin Trulsson
abstract:
Author(s): Pappu Acharya and Martin Trulsson

Alternating shear rotations in dense suspensions have recently shown the ability to reduce both viscosity and dissipation per strain (at a fixed global shear rate). Here, we study alternating shear rotations, with extensive numerical simulations, at various angles and up to their corresponding jammi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033013] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shear jamming transitions in dense suspensions under alternating shear rotations.
motivation: Understanding how alternating shear rotations affect viscosity and dissipation in dense suspensions is important for controlling flow and jamming behavior.
method: The authors perform extensive numerical simulations of frictional and frictionless suspensions under alternating shear rotations at various angles.
result: They observe a shear jamming transition and find that alternating rotations can reduce viscosity and dissipation per strain.
conclusion: Alternating shear rotations offer a way to tune rheological properties of dense suspensions, with potential applications in material processing.

title: Focusing Characteristics Of Cylindrically Bent Laue Crystals
authors: Yu-Hang Wang, Ming Li, And Quan-Jie Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hang Wang, Ming Li, and Quan-Jie Jia

An analytical wave-optical framework for cylindrically bent Laue crystals is developed from the Takagi-Taupin theory. The framework separates geometric, kinematical, and higher-order scattering contributions and provides monochromatic and polychromatic focusing conditions together with a conservation relation describing aperture effects


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032001] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical wave-optical framework for cylindrically bent Laue crystals, focusing on X-ray focusing characteristics.
motivation: To provide a theoretical understanding of focusing properties of bent Laue crystals used in X-ray optics.
method: The framework is derived from the Takagi-Taupin theory, separating geometric, kinematical, and higher-order scattering contributions.
result: Monochromator and polychromatic focusing conditions are derived, along with a conservation relation describing aperture effects.
conclusion: The framework offers a comprehensive analytical tool for designing and optimizing bent Laue crystal optics.

title: Positron Transport And Cooling With ${\mathrm{CF}}_{4}$ In An Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
authors: J. von der Linden, A. Deller, S. Nißl, K. Michishio, H. Higaki, And E. V. Stenson
abstract:
Author(s): J. von der Linden, A. Deller, S. Nißl, K. Michishio, H. Higaki, and E. V. Stenson

Time-resolved measurements of positrons confined in a magnetic dipole trap and interacting with CF
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032002] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies positron transport and cooling in CF4 gas within an inhomogeneous magnetic field, focusing on loss channels and scattering dynamics.
motivation: Understanding positron cooling and transport is important for applications like positronium formation and antimatter studies, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved measurements of positrons in a magnetic dipole trap with CF4 gas, using gamma-ray annihilation spectra and ramped ejection to distinguish trapped populations.
result: A transition from positronium formation to cross-field transport as the dominant loss channel occurs when positrons cool below the charge-exchange threshold.
conclusion: The study characterizes positron cooling dynamics in CF4, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rheology And Yielding Of Charged Vesicle Gels: Experiments And Simulations
authors: N. Kolezakis, R. Pastore, F. Rusciano, V. Guida, P. L. Maffettone, And G. D'avino
abstract:

The behavior of charged vesicle suspensions, commonly encountered in biological and industrial contexts, is largely governed by screened electrostatic repulsions. result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques and optical antennas.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with tip-enhanced optical fluorescence, where the tip acts as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals and X-ray pulse profiles, and compares them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Provides updated constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities.
conclusion: Neutron star observations continue to improve our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, projecting sensitivities for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures, but does not present new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain regions, and the HL-LHC will significantly extend the search reach, but no definitive discovery is guaranteed.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review three real-space techniques that provide direct access to such information.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights the capabilities and limitations of each technique and demonstrates how combining them yields a more comprehensive understanding of disorder.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques are powerful for characterizing atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, and their combination offers the most complete picture.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but many reactions have very small rates and are difficult to measure directly.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions on Earth.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the current theoretical understanding and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand the quantum physics underlying stellar nuclear reactions.

conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical calculations.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches.

tldr: This paper measures the propulsive force of a eukaryotic swimmer (Chlamydomonas) using optical tweezers, finding that swimming speed is not a direct proxy for force output.
motivation: To directly measure the propulsive force of a microscopic swimmer and test the assumption that swimming speed is a proxy for motor force.
method: Optical tweezers were used to trap a single Chlamydomonas cell and measure the force exerted by its flagella during swimming.
result: The propulsive force was found to be approximately 0.3 pN, and the relationship between swimming speed and force is not linear, indicating that speed is not a reliable proxy for force.
conclusion: Direct force measurements reveal that swimming kinematics do not accurately reflect motor force output in eukaryotic swimmers, challenging a common assumption in biophysics.

abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy astrophysical emission from the Galactic Center, focusing on the supermassive black hole and surrounding structures.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength overview of the high-energy phenomena in the Galactic Center, which is the closest and best-studied galactic nucleus.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths, including X-rays, gamma rays, and radio, summarizing known sources and processes.
result: The Galactic Center hosts a supermassive black hole with quiescent and flaring emission, plasma bubbles, X-ray chimneys, and a dense molecular zone.
conclusion: The region is a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysical processes, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Understanding vacuum breakdown is crucial for improving the reliability and efficiency of particle accelerators, fusion reactors, and other high-power technologies.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and computational studies to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights could help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent advances from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The field continues to advance with high-precision data from BESIII, contributing to our understanding of strong interaction dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's planetary radar was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper is a historical review of radio astronomy achievements at the Arecibo Observatory, with no connection to quantum information theory or quantum technologies.
motivation: The paper aims to document Arecibo's legacy in radio astronomy, covering pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
method: It is a colloquium-style review summarizing historical developments and scientific contributions from Arecibo's five decades of operation.
result: The paper highlights Arecibo's major contributions across diverse astrophysical topics, but does not present new research or technical results.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific impact, but the paper is purely historical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made with the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere have enabled significant advances in geospace science, but these results are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar technique and presents key findings from Arecibo's suite of instruments in plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, atomic metal layers, and coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been a vital tool for geospace research, but the paper does not contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves from neutron stars are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications of multimessenger observations for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics and astrophysics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide insights into turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, helping to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully explain the rapid transition.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on detection and parameter estimation.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would provide unique multimessenger insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The authors summarize recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discuss detection methods using ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The paper presents the latest modeling and detection strategies for gravitational waves from core collapse supernovae.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova will enable multimessenger studies of the central engine and neutron star formation.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on radio galaxy and quasar catalogs.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to assess the compatibility of the matter dipole with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM interpretation.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on dark matter halos.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical predictions and observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental advances over the last decade in nuclear reaction rates, plasma and atomic physics, and solar modeling.
result: It summarizes updated nuclear reaction rates and their impact on solar models, including comparisons with neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent progress in solar fusion physics, providing a benchmark for stellar evolution models.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, focusing on fluid mechanics.
result: Key insights include the effects of added mass, deformable surfaces, turbulence, and surfactants on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive overview to guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
